item.title: Why was Cole Palmer sent off against Tottenham?
item.description: Cole Palmer was sent off as Chelsea experienced a late capitulation to suffer their first home defeat to Tottenham since 2018. The Blues fell behind in the 78th minute when 21-year-old goalkeeping understudy Mike Penders, making his full Premier League debut in the absence of the injured Emi Martinez, punched into his own net from a corner in the 78th minute. Things then went from bad to worse for Xabi Alonso ’s side in the pouring rain, with Blues talisman Palmer catching former team-mate and Chelsea youth product Conor Gallagher as he brought down a Spurs free-kick. Palmer’s studs caught the ankle of the midfielder, who had replaced James Maddison after he suffered another gut-wrenching injury setback in a Tottenham shirt. Cole Palmer leaves the field after being sent off against Tottenham (Getty) Palmer and Chelsea players vigorously appealed for the decision to be overturned, which VAR does now have the power to do with second yellow cards. But Chris Kavanagh stuck with his decision and Chelsea were reduced to 10 men. Palmer will now miss Chelsea’s trip to Liverpool for the Carabao Cup. Palmer picked up his first yellow in similarly-dramatic circumstances, barging into a kneeled Mateus Fernandes with his torso after the Portuguese midfielder committed a cynical foul, pawing the bawl away while downed to stop Chelsea charging on goal. A scuffle ensued which saw Fernandes and Micky van de Ven also booked. Tottenham put the seal on a 2-0 victory seven minutes after Palmer’s dismissal, with Mathys Tel finishing off a superb individual goal to wrap up Spurs’ first triumph on Chelsea soil 2018.

item.title: Holy Cross senior Dae'Sean Graves breaks Connecticut's career record for TD receptions
item.description: WATERBURY - Holy Cross High senior wide receiver Dae'Sean Graves came into Saturday morning's game at Crosby one touchdown catch away from tying the state's all-time career record, and two away from breaking it. It took a little bit of time, but the UConn commit caught touchdowns of 37 and 6 yards from senior quarterback Brady Lombardo to become the state record holder with 51 career touchdown receptions. Holy Cross beat Crosby 52-13 and improved to 5-1. No one has caught more touchdowns in the history of Connecticut high school football than Holy Cross WR Dae'Sean Graves. The senior caught his 50th and 51st touchdown on Saturday in the Crusaders' 52-13 win over Crosby. His 51st TD reception moved him past Southington's Alex Jamele, who set the record in 2014. Graves had 8 catches in the game and is now 11 catches away from setting the state record for receptions in a career. #cthsfb #connecticut #highschoolfootball (Pete Paguaga/Hearst Connecticut Media) Graves broke Southington star Alex Jamele's former record of 50, set in 2014, by catching two touchdowns in the final minutes of the first half. After a fumble recovery by the Crusader defense, Graves went deep and Lombardo hit him for a 37-yard touchdown pass with 2:24 left in the second quarter to tie Jamele's record. Holy Cross got the ball back with 50.1 seconds left in the first half, and Graves caught a 33-yard pass from Lombardo to get the ball to the Crosby 6-yard line. After an incomplete pass, Graves came in motion, moving from right to left. Lombardo caught the snap and pitched it forward to Graves on a jet pass. Graves broke a tackle at the goal line to score and break Jamele's record. Holy Cross' Dae'Sean Graves (1) runs in a shuttle pass for a touchdown against Crosby to break the state record for career TD receptions Saturday, Oct. 23, 2026, at Crosby High School in Waterbury. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) The entire Crusader offensive unit joined Graves in the end zone to celebrate. Graves finished with eight catches for 132 yards and the two touchdowns, and all of it came in the first half. He is 10 catches away from tying East Catholic star Joey Montalvo's state record of 226, which was set last year. Graves now has 3,229 career receiving yards, which puts him 642 yards away from tying Montalvo's record of 3,871, which was also set last year. As if Graves didn't have a big enough morning, he also returned an interception 39 yards for a touchdown. Freshman Anthony Serrano also had an interception return for a score for Holy Cross. Besides the two touchdowns to Graves, Lombardo threw scoring passes of 68 yards to Aaden Hall and 10 yards to Tyler Smith. Raquim Chapman scored the first touchdown of the game on a 1-yard sneak for Crosby (2-4). Kayden Myers ran for a 17-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. Player of the Game Dae'Sean Graves, Holy Cross: The senior wide receiver caught two touchdown passes to break Alex Jamele's all-time state record for career scoring recep

item.title: How Astros can make trade for Marlins' Cy Young 'without issue'
item.description: How Astros can make trade for Marlins' Cy Young 'without issue' originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Astros could use another frontline starting pitcher. Hunter Brown is the AL West club's ace, but the Astros lack solid rotational depth after Peter Lamber's breakout season. Even without a new general manager, the Astros should be busy this offseason. They need at least one outfielder and one starter, if not multiple. FanSided's Jake Elman wrote that the Astros could target Miami Marlins ace Sandy Alcantara. However, the Marlins may prefer to keep Alcantara as they look to compete for a postseason berth in 2027. "We’re honestly not sure whether the Marlins would trade Alcantara, who has a $21 million club option with a $1 million trade assignment bonus. He had an impressive bounce-back season in 2026 with a 3.87 ERA, his lowest since his 2022 NL Cy Young campaign, and he looked more confident as the season progressed," Elman wrote. Alcantara isn't racking up strikeouts like he used to, punching out just 17.1% of the batters he faced in 2026. Still, he was a workhorse, finishing the season with a Major League high of 214 innings. MORE : Dodgers facing tricky question over Shohei Ohtani's future as a two-way player "Alcantara just turned 31, and he’d slot in behind Hunter Brown as the Astros’ No. 2 pitcher. We should also note he doesn’t have a no-trade clause, so the penny-pinching Marlins could part ways with him without issue," Elman added. The Astros don't have to jump through hoops if they'd like to acquire Alcantara to be their No. 2 starter. As detailed, he does not have a no-trade clause in his contract. Houston's front office should definitley target rotation upgrades this winter, and Alcantara is an intriguing option who will earn a reasonable $21 million next season. item.title: Gamethread: Boston College vs Georgia Tech
item.description: CHESTNUT HILL, MA - OCTOBER 17: Boston College Eagles take the field prior to college football game between Pittsburgh Panthers and Boston College Eagles on October 17, 2026, at Alumni Stadium in Chestnut Hill, MA. (Photo by M. Anthony Nesmith/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We’re almost underway here at Bobby Dodd Stadium. The Eagles are looking to build on last week’s performance with another conference win and getting within striking distance of a bowl appearance (look at us, who would’ve thought). The Jackets, meanwhile, are trying to avoid the bottom falling out. They put together a solid second half especially on offense, and are fully capable of putting up points if they can get over some red zone struggles. Defensively, they’ve struggled to get off the field, so they can’t afford their offense to not keep pace. The Eagles will be without start running g back Evan Dickens, who is out for the season after injury last weekend. Georgia Tech lead running back Justice Haynes will return, but two key defensive pieces are likely out. I’m expecting a close one here, but BC is every bit capable of pulling out the win with the way the defense has looked and with McKenzie’s baller-ness. Who: Boston College Eagles (3-3) vs Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets (2-4) Where: When: Saturday October 24, 2026 Kickoff Time: 3:30 pm Atlanta, Georgia How to Watch: This game will be live on ACC Network

item.title: F1 United States GP: Lewis Hamilton pips Max Verstappen in FP3
item.description: Motorsport photo Lewis Hamilton finished final practice on top at Formula 1's United States Grand Prix, leading Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc into qualifying at Austin. Hamilton was the only driver to break the 1m35s barrier in the final 20 minutes of third practice, as frequent track limits transgressions kept Ferrari team-mate Leclerc from leapfrogging him on the leaderboard. Following an opening quarter of the session which can only be described as pedestrian, action picked up as Hamilton set a 1m36.716s on softs to get ahead of a number of medium-tyred install laps. His time was soon beaten by Liam Lawson in the Racing Bulls and McLaren's Oscar Piastri , while several heavy hitters kept turning laps on medium tyres instead. Verstappen even went top courtesy of a 1m35.702s on the yellow sidewall tyre, despite recurring complaints about his unsettling downshifts. Hamilton swiftly improved upon the Dutchman's lap, using softs to set a 1m35.561s. But when Leclerc took over command with a 1m35.127s despite using the slower mediums, that underlined there was still a lot more pace to find. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Entering the final 20 minutes, Antonelli took a tenth out of Leclerc's time on softs, but his lap was scratched for breaking track limits at Turn 9. Verstappen did adhere to the white lines to set a 1m35.061s and go top, with Red Bull the quickest car through sector one, only for Hamilton to dip below the 1m35s barrier with a 1m34.893s. Track limits, which have been a recurring theme throughout practice, also kept Leclerc from reclaiming first as he dipped over the white line at Turn 10. That meant the Monegasque had to settle for third behind Hamilton and Verstappen, setting up a finely poised qualifying session on Saturday afternoon. Championship leader Antonelli was fourth ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell , as the Silver Arrows appears to be a half-step behind on pure pace, with Piastri sixth in the difficult to tame MCL40. In the Audi , Nico Hulkenberg kept McLaren ’s Lando Norris from seventh, with the world champion’s 1m35.2s also deleted for track limits at Turn 10. Alpine driver Pierre Gasly was ninth, a full second behind Hamilton, with Isack Hadjar 10th in the second Red Bull as the Frenchman was left frustrated by his car's handling. item.title: UFC 333 Highlights! Pico Delivers Blistering 74-Second TKO Over Keita
item.description: ABU DHABI, UNITED ARAB EMIRATES - OCTOBER 24: Aaron Pico reacts after a victory against Losene Keita of Guinea in a featherweight fight during the UFC 333 event at Etihad Arena on October 24, 2026 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Aaron Pico finally lived up to his billing earlier today (Sat., Oct. 24, 2026) at UFC 333 LIVE on Paramount+ from inside Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, as the featherweight contender stunned Losene Keita with an early first-round TKO (punches). Pico has always carried the potential to fight for a world title, but the former Bellator MMA star just hasn’t put it all together. Fight fans were hoping a move to UFC’s big stage would open a new level to Pico’s game. Before Saturday’s main event opener against Keita, Pico hadn’t shown he’s ready for the top featherweights in the world. It took him only 74 seconds to change that and put himself back into the top 10 mix heading into 2027. Pico, who was coming off his first UFC win with a decision over Patricio Pitbull last April, used his wrestling in the opening moments of the first and scored a nice takedown. His top pressure didn’t last long, but Pico’s level change still had Keita guessing. That allowed Pico the chance to utilize his striking and he ended up landing a stinging right hand. Keita was hurt and stumbled backwards before falling to the canvas. Pico jumped on top for some brief ground-and-pound before he referee stepped in. After the win, Pico took to the microphone and called out his fellow featherweights who refused to fight him Pico referenced them as “rankings squatter.” Check out the knockout finish and Pico’s post-fight interview below: AARON PICO KNOCKS OUT KEITA IN RD 1!!! Aaron Pico is ready for the next challenge! item.title: Juventus Women 2-5 Roma | Match Report
item.description: Juventus Women 2-5 Roma | Match Report Juventus Women suffered a 5-2 defeat to Roma on Matchday 4 of Serie A Women. At the Pozzo-La Marmora Stadium in Biella, the visitors took control of the match in the first half. The Bianconere responded after the break, pulling two goals back through Redondo and Pavan, but were unable to complete the comeback. ROMA MAKE A STRONG START Roma started brightly and broke the deadlock after just four minutes, with Giugliano finding the net from distance. The visitors doubled their lead in the 10th minute through Pellegrino Cimò, who was set up by Rieke, before Corelli made it 3-0 three minutes later, getting ahead of Carbonell to score from a free-kick delivery. Juventus looked to respond and came close in the 18th minute when Salvai's header was saved by Baldi. Five minutes later, Sarriegi tried to find space inside the Roma penalty area but was denied by a defensive intervention from Oladipo. The Bianconere threatened again towards the end of the half, with Chiba testing Baldi with a left-footed effort in the 45th minute. However, deep into stoppage time, Roma were awarded a penalty for a Pinto handball, with the decision confirmed following an FVS review. Giugliano made no mistake from the spot to send the visitors into the break with a 4-0 lead. THE BIANCONERE FIGHT BACK AFTER THE BREAK Juventus made two changes at half-time, with Noordman and Pavan replacing Chiba and Sarriegi, as the Bianconere looked to change the momentum of the match. Roma thought they had added a fifth goal four minutes into the second half through Pellegrino Cimò, but the effort was ruled out for offside. Five minutes later, Juventus pulled a goal back: Noordman delivered a low cross into the box and Redondo was on hand to turn the ball home and make it 4-1. The Bianconere continued to push forward and came close to scoring again in the 69th minute through Librán, who had replaced Bartel shortly before. The midfielder controlled the ball inside the area before firing narrowly over the crossbar. Juventus found their second goal in the 77th minute, with Redondo turning provider for Pavan, who finished to reduce the deficit to two goals. Isaac Guerrero's side kept pressing and almost added a third in the 87th minute, when Redondo's header flew just over the bar. However, a minute later, Bergamaschi found the net to make it 5-2 and seal the victory for Roma. Juventus were ultimately left empty-handed after a match shaped by Roma's strong first-half display and the Bianconere's response after the break. Women | Juventus-Roma | Gallery

item.title: Demichelis and Baumgartner happy to "get back to winning ways" against Elversberg
item.description: Demichelis and Baumgartner happy to "get back to winning ways" against Elversberg A resounding 4-0 win over SC Elversberg earlier today was more than enough reason for Martin Demichelis to smile after their day's work. "After two defeats, we had to get back to winning ways today. We were up against a tricky opponent and the first half wasn't easy. “The changes we made helped us match their intensity, and our quality made the difference in front of goal,” Demichelis said after the game. "A lot of people probably thought I was taking too much of a risk [with 8 changes]. But five of the players in today's line-up also played in Munich a week ago. “I see how hard they work in training. Keeping a clean sheet was important too,” the Argentine explained with a smile. Making his return from a long-term injury layoff, Christoph Baumgartner was another happy face soaking up the win in the mixed zone. “First of all, huge credit to Elversberg. They're doing an incredible job and they caused us quite a few problems. "We made a few adjustments at half time and did a better job of finding space in front of their defence and making runs in behind. We've also got the individual quality to make the difference. Getting that first goal was crucial.” “After such a memorable moment for me personally at the Bernabéu, I was really looking forward to playing at home again. "The most important thing is that we won, but to come back after so long and score straight away is pretty cool," the Austria concluded. Leipzig's attention will now turn to preparations for their DFB-Pokal second round fixture away to Rot Weiss Essen next Tuesday.

item.title: UFC 333 video: Aaron Pico smashes Losene Keita with devastating 1st round knockout
item.description: ABU DHABI, UNITED ARAB EMIRATES - OCTOBER 24: Aaron Pico punches Losene Keita of Guinea in a featherweight fight during the UFC 333 event at Etihad Arena on October 24, 2026 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Aaron Pico officially has his first finish in the octagon after he scored a lightning quick knockout over Losene Keita to open the UFC 333 main card. Pico wasted no time using his wrestling to keep Keita off balance but then he unleashed a beautiful straight right hand that put the former Oktagon champion down on the round. Pico followed him there and continued dishing out punishment until the referee saw enough to stop the fight. AARON PICO KNOCKS OUT KEITA IN RD 1!!! [ #UFC333 | LIVE on @paramountplus ] pic.twitter.com/0fl49WEHgY — UFC on Paramount+ (@UFConParamount) October 24, 2026 The end came at just 1:14 into the opening round. “Honestly it feels amazing,’ Pico said about his win. “I’ve been wrestling since I was four years old. I told my coaches after this fight he going to wish he put on he wrestling shoes since he was four years old. “I want a rematch with Lerone Murphy … I want to make money, I want to get to the title.” Pico opened the fight with a perfectly timed single-leg takdown to put Keita on his back. Pico then transitioned into some ground and pound but Keita scrambled to get back to his feet to reset the fight. Pico then unleashed a brutal right hand that put Keita down on the canvas and the American quickly followed him to the floor where he continued the assault. The shots were coming hard and heavy with Pico punching away and Keita face down on the ground. The punches kept raining down and the referee saw enough to stop the fight before further damage was dished out. Pico has now won back-to-back fights after his knockout loss to Lerone Murphy in his debut. The highly touted featherweight is now looking for higher ranked competition and it’s going to be hard to deny him after performances like this one.

item.title: Lewis Hamilton tops the timing sheets in FP3 ahead of Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc
item.description: (Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images) | Getty Images AUSTIN, Texas — Lewis Hamilton topped the timing sheets in the third and final hour of practice ahead of Max Verstappen and teammate Charles Leclerc, setting up what could be a dramatic qualifying hour here at the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix. The session got underway right at 12:30 p.m. local time, under partly cloudy skies with the air temperature right at 80 degrees Fahrenheit. And a few teams did not waste any time, with Sergio Pérez, Gabriel Bortoleto, and Franco Colapinto taking to the track right as the green light appeared at the end of pit lane. A few other teams, however, took a more relaxed approach at the start, as drivers such as Lando Norris, Verstappen, Oscar Piastri, Leclerc, and Oliver Bearman remained in the garage, waiting to take to the track. And when Bortoleto dipped back down pit lane, Pérez and Colapinto had the track to themselves. Gasly soon joined the fray, as did Valtteri Bottas, and as the clock struck 53 minutes remaining the Cadillac and Alpine duos had the track all to themselves. Things started to pick up at the 50-minute mark, as more cars took to the track. Soon some more representative times would be coming in, as at the 47-minute mark Gasly topped the timing sheets with a 1:37.592, a time set on the C3 medium tire. Hamilton then took that spot with a 1:36.716, posted on a set of softs, as the times started to come in, and tumble. The first big surprises came with around 43 minutes left in FP3, as Liam Lawson jumped to the top of the timing sheets with a 1:36.420, set on a set of C3 medium tires. His spot at the top would not last long as Piastri nipped him with a 1:36.243 on the softs, and then Max Verstappen pumped in a 1:35.702 on the mediums. Hamilton then responded, delivering a lap of 1:35.561 to rocket to the top of the board. At the midpoint of FP2 the top five on the board were Hamilton, Verstappen, Norris, George Russell, and Isack Hadjar. While the teams and names might not be a surprise, the tire choices might have been. While Hamilton, Norris, and Russell set those times on the C4 soft tires, Hadjar and Verstappen had set those on the C3 mediums. That spoke to the pace with the RB22 for both Saturday … and Sunday. Two more names entered the mix as the second half of FP3 opened. Leclerc went to the top on a set of medium tires – perhaps speaking to both Ferrari’s pace and the small upgrades the team brought to Austin – and then Drivers’ Championship leader Kimi Antonelli slid into third, on a set of the soft tires. Things did get a little sporty at one moment, with Russell, Esteban Ocon, and Nico Hülkenberg treating the proceedings like Sunday rather than Saturday: Getting a little too close for comfort 😬 Russell, Ocon and Hulkenberg get some racing practice in during FP3 ⚔️ #F1 #USGP pic.twitter.com/D6uX1pY4WY — Formula 1 (@F1) October 24, 2026 At the 20-minute mark, many of the top drivers were in the garage, including the Ferrari pair as wel
item.content:encoded: (Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images) | Getty Images AUSTIN, Texas — Lewis Hamilton topped the timing sheets in the third and final hour of practice ahead of Max Verstappen and teammate Charles Leclerc, setting up what could be a dramatic qualifying hour here at the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix. The session got underway right at 12:30 p.m. local time, under partly cloudy skies with the air temperature right at 80 degrees Fahrenheit. And a few teams did not waste any time, with Sergio Pérez, Gabriel Bortoleto, and Franco Colapinto taking to the track right as the green light appeared at the end of pit lane. A few other teams, however, took a more relaxed approach at the start, as drivers such as Lando Norris, Verstappen, Oscar Piastri, Leclerc, and Oliver Bearman remained in the garage, waiting to take to the track. And when Bortoleto dipped back down pit lane, Pérez and Colapinto had the track to themselves. Gasly soon joined the fray, as did Valtteri Bottas, and as the clock struck 53 minutes remaining the Cadillac and Alpine duos had the track all to themselves. Things started to pick up at the 50-minute mark, as more cars took to the track. Soon some more representative times would be coming in, as at the 47-minute mark Gasly topped the timing sheets with a 1:37.592, a time set on the C3 medium tire. Hamilton then took that spot with a 1:36.716, posted on a set of softs, as the times started to come in, and tumble. The first big surprises came with around 43 minutes left in FP3, as Liam Lawson jumped to the top of the timing sheets with a 1:36.420, set on a set of C3 medium tires. His spot at the top would not last long as Piastri nipped him with a 1:36.243 on the softs, and then Max Verstappen pumped in a 1:35.702 on the mediums. Hamilton then responded, delivering a lap of 1:35.561 to rocket to the top of the board. At the midpoint of FP2 the top five on the board were Hamilton, Verstappen, Norris, George Russell, and Isack Hadjar. While the teams and names might not be a surprise, the tire choices might have been. While Hamilton, Norris, and Russell set those times on the C4 soft tires, Hadjar and Verstappen had set those on the C3 mediums. That spoke to the pace with the RB22 for both Saturday … and Sunday. Two more names entered the mix as the second half of FP3 opened. Leclerc went to the top on a set of medium tires – perhaps speaking to both Ferrari’s pace and the small upgrades the team brought to Austin – and then Drivers’ Championship leader Kimi Antonelli slid into third, on a set of the soft tires. Things did get a little sporty at one moment, with Russell, Esteban Ocon, and Nico Hülkenberg treating the proceedings like Sunday rather than Saturday: Getting a little too close for comfort 😬 Russell, Ocon and Hulkenberg get some racing practice in during FP3 ⚔️ #F1 #USGP pic.twitter.com/D6uX1pY4WY — Formula 1 (@F1) October 24, 2026 At the 20-minute mark, many of the top drivers were in the garage, including the Ferrari pair as well as Verstappen and the McLaren duo. But Antonelli was in full attack mode, using a fresh set of C4 soft tires that had been bolted onto his W17. Behind him? His Mercedes teammate Russell, also with a fresh set of soft tires. Antonelli went purple through the first sector and purple through the second as he tracked 0.414 second ahead of the benchmark time set by Leclerc. He came home with a lap time of 1:35.015, a new benchmark and a clear warning to the rest of the grid. But it was for naught, as his time was deleted for exceeding track limits at Turn 9. Then it was Verstappen’s turn, as Red Bull bolted a set of soft tires onto his RB22. He went fastest through the first sector, and was still up on Leclerc through the second sector. Verstappen came home with a time of 1:35.061, setting a new standard for the session. That standard lasted only a few seconds, as Hamilton cut the beam with a 1:34.893. Finally we got a representative lap on the softs from Leclerc, and it put Ferrari’s other driver to the top, as he delivered a 1:34.810, just ahead of Hamilton in P2. However, that lap was soon deleted as well, with Leclerc having exceeded track limits at Turn 10. Track limits might be something to watch during qualifying later today, after an astonishing 207 lap times were deleted over the two practice sessions on Friday, and race officials relaxed track limits at several spots on the track, including Turns 12, 15 and 20. With under ten minutes remaining, perhaps the biggest surprise was the driver sitting in P7 as it was none other than Hülkenberg sitting well inside the top ten. Could he and Audi be setting up a Q3 shock for later in the day? Hülkenberg might, but his teammate could be in a bit of hot water, as race officials noted Gabriel Bortoleto for potentially impeding Hamilton during a push lap in the final minutes of the session. And in those final minutes of the session, there was a bit of drama from the Red Bull pair. First it was from Verstappen as he locked up his RB22 entering Turn 15, and sent smoke flying on the track as he flat-spotted the tires. Then it was Hadjar locking up at Turn 1, as he came upon Alexander Albon on the racing line. The two drivers had a bit of a … moment on the track before driving off their separate ways. When the checkered flag flew, it was still Hamilton at the top of the board, followed by Verstappen, Leclerc, Antonelli, and Russell rounding out the top five. Piastri slotted in sixth, followed by Hülkenberg, Norris, Gasly, and Hadjar to close out the top ten spots. Liam Lawson clocked in at P11, followed by teammate Arvid Lindblad in P12. Bortoleto, Bearman, Colapinto, Alonso, Ocon, Stroll, Albon, Sainz, Pérez, and Bottas rounded out the rest of the grid. What does this all mean for qualifying later today? It might mean we’ll have a shootout on our hands here in Austin.

item.title: 104-year-old Brewers fan makes second accurate score prediction
item.description: Charlotte Werning Kolby thinks she should be placing bets. Her 104-year-old mother Ruth Werning has now accurately predicted the Milwaukee Brewers' winning score not once, but twice, on their post-season journey. First, Werning told a WISN-TV reporter the Brewers would win 6-2 in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers Oct. 14. She was right. Days later, Werning told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel her World Series Game 1 prediction: Brewers would beat the Tampa Bay Devil Rays, 3-2. For a few seconds of Friday night's chaotic ninth inning , some of the Brewers players, an umpire, a broadcaster, thousands of fans and, apparently, whoever controls American Family Field's post-game fireworks, would have said Werning's Game 1 prediction was off. They all thought shortstop Cooper Pratt caught the ball with his foot still on second base before turning a double-play to secure a 3-1 win and take a 1-0 series lead. But Werning was right after all, even if it caused the 43,250 fans in attendance and Brewers Nation a few more tense minutes. But after a challenge on the play from Rays manager Kevin Cash, a replay showed Pratt's foot came off second base. Then Brewers pitcher Trevor Megill struck out Jonny DeLuca to actually close out the game, and the Brewers won 3-2, just as Werning predicted. "I wish I were a betting person," daughter Werning Kolby said the morning after World Series Game 1. Her mom didn't get her Game 4 NLCS prediction right, but still, these two correct predictions are "more than kind of crazy," Werning Kolby said. Ruth Werning didn't stay up to watch the end of Game 1. Werning woke up "on cloud nine" about her Milwaukee Brewers winning, according to her daughter, who checked in with her mom on the phone during breakfast. The pair are still game to attend a Brewers World Series game in person, if the opportunity presents itself. Werning doesn't make predictions like this often, her daughter said. But she does have a strong intuition. "She's got a hotline to God, I'll tell you that," Werning Kolby the morning of Oct. 24. So, what does Werning guess will happen in Game 2 of the World Series? Werning Kolby relayed her mom's prediction over the phone. "They will win, and the score will be 3-1 Brewers," Werning Kolby said. She said her mom sounded quite confident. This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: 104-year-old Brewers fan makes second accurate score prediction

item.title: Packers fan survey says Christian Watson will finish 2026 as top receiver
item.description: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 16: Christian Watson #9 and Matthew Golden #0 of the Green Bay Packers line up before a play during an NFL football game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on November 16, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matthew Golden, drops aside, is on a hot streak. He has hit the century mark in receiving yardage in two straight games and has nearly closed the gap on Christian Watson for the team lead in receiving yards. Watson still has a slight edge, but both players are over 500 yards on the season, making them the only receiver tandem in the NFL to have reached that mark after Week 6. But will that success continue? We asked Packers fans this week which player was the one they thought would finish the season as the team’s leader in receiving yardage. While Golden got a substantial share of the vote, Watson still came out on top with 61% of the responses favoring him over Golden. The second-year pro received a solid 36 percent vote share, however, with “other” coming in at just three percent. Here’s a look at the results: It seems that sportsbooks are extremely evenly split on who they expect to be the Packers’ WR1 to be moving forward. For the Packers’ Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions, FanDuel Sportsbook has the over/unders on receiving yards set extremely closely: Christian Watson’s number is 74.5, while Golden is one yard short of that number at 73.5. As for overall fan confidence, the win over the Cowboys has Packers fans continuing to tick upward in their general sentiments. After last week’s confidence index grew back over 50 percent for the first time since early in the season, that number is now up to 76% with the Lions on deck. Keep it here at APC for full coverage of Sunday’s game in Detroit to see if the Packers can keep their winning streak going.

The match is part of the 32nd round of the league and takes place at Maião stadium, in the interior of São Paulo state. Mirassol are looking for a win to move even further clear of the relegation zone. Meanwhile, São Paulo still hope to secure a place in next year's Libertadores. See the starting lineups below: São Paulo Forwards Calleri and Artur are ruled out of the match due to fitness issues. Lucas Moura makes his first start since recovering from his latest injury. item.title: Spalletti could be two games away from the sack at Juventus
item.description: Spalletti could be two games away from the sack at Juventus Juventus cannot afford to spend another season without Champions League football, and the club could be ready to dismiss Luciano Spalletti if results fail to improve. The Bianconeri are determined to secure a place among Serie A’s top four, and continued inconsistency could force the hierarchy to consider a change in the dugout. Spalletti has now spent around a year on the Juventus bench, and this is his first full season in charge of the club. Expectations remain high, with the manager expected to deliver consistent victories and guide the team towards its objectives. However, Juventus have struggled to maintain the required level of performance, leaving his position under increasing pressure. The club needs a strong response from its players, but the responsibility also rests with Spalletti to find solutions and restore confidence. With Champions League qualification such an important target, Juventus may have little patience if their results continue to disappoint. Juventus consider their managerial options The Bianconeri have been linked with potential moves for Antonio Conte and Simone Inzaghi in recent weeks. Both managers have considerable experience at the highest level, and their names have emerged as possible alternatives should Juventus decide to make a change. The Old Lady has shown that it is willing to dismiss managers when performances fall below expectations. That history means Spalletti cannot assume his position is secure, particularly with the club facing an important period in its campaign. According to a report involving Giuseppe Falci, Juventus could decide to sack Spalletti if the results of their next two matches fail to meet expectations. The upcoming fixtures could therefore prove decisive for the manager as he attempts to keep the club on course for its objectives. (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images) Two matches could decide Spalletti’s future Juventus face Lecce and Genoa in their next two games, both away from home. These are fixtures the club will expect to win if it is serious about securing a place in the Serie A top four by the end of the season. Failure to collect the required points in either match would increase the pressure, while disappointing results in both could leave the club considering an immediate managerial change. Spalletti will therefore understand the importance of producing positive performances and results. Falci discussed the situation via Tuttojuve , stating: “Spalletti’s future hangs on the next two matches, both away: Lecce and Genoa.”

item.title: Eddie Howe can repeat his genius Joelinton masterstroke with this Man United star waiting to be unleashed
item.description: Eddie Howe can repeat his genius Joelinton masterstroke with this Man United star waiting to be unleashed Fabian Hürzeler has dismissed speculation that he is set to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United. At the same time, Antonio Conte has insisted that claims of him being in talks with a top club are unfounded and that he is not pushing for an immediate return to management. United, for their part, are not keen on Conte, with reports suggesting Ineos do not view him as the right fit for their project. Should Carrick be dismissed, however, the contest now feels like a two-horse race between Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann . While Nagelsmann’s tactical sharpness could make him an upgrade on Carrick, if I were calling the shots, I would still opt for Howe. Why Eddie Howe? Howe is Premier League proven. At Bournemouth, he kept the club in the top flight for five consecutive seasons, a remarkable achievement that earned him Football League Manager of the Decade . At Newcastle, he restored the club’s competitive edge and gave them a clear identity. He eventually guided them back into the Champions League for the first time in 20 years. At both clubs, he established himself as one of the most successful managers of their modern eras. The main argument against Howe is that, while he might fix what is broken at United, just as he did at Newcastle, he may lack the final ingredient needed to push the team over the line and deliver a 21st league title. Critics are quick to point out that he never transformed Newcastle into genuine title challengers. Yet that argument is illogical. Despite having some of the richest owners in world football, Newcastle often struggled in the transfer market. Howe wanted the very front three United now possess, Matheus Cunha , Benjamin Šeško and Bryan Mbeumo , but all three rejected the chance to join him. As a result, the Toons endured one of their most disappointing summer windows in 2025. Had Howe secured those players and avoided the injury problems that followed, Newcastle’s 2025-26 campaign could have looked very different. If Jason Wilcox goes ahead and hires Howe, fans will naturally look to him to get the best out of Cunha, Mbeumo and Šeško. Still, one player I believe could be massively revitalised is Joshua Zirkzee . item.content:encoded: Eddie Howe can repeat his genius Joelinton masterstroke with this Man United star waiting to be unleashed Fabian Hürzeler has dismissed speculation that he is set to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United. At the same time, Antonio Conte has insisted that claims of him being in talks with a top club are unfounded and that he is not pushing for an immediate return to management. United, for their part, are not keen on Conte, with reports suggesting Ineos do not view him as the right fit for their project. Should Carrick be dismissed, however, the contest now feels like a two-horse race between Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann . While Nagelsmann’s tactical sharpness could make him an upgrade on Carrick, if I were calling the shots, I would still opt for Howe. Why Eddie Howe? Howe is Premier League proven. At Bournemouth, he kept the club in the top flight for five consecutive seasons, a remarkable achievement that earned him Football League Manager of the Decade . At Newcastle, he restored the club’s competitive edge and gave them a clear identity. He eventually guided them back into the Champions League for the first time in 20 years. At both clubs, he established himself as one of the most successful managers of their modern eras. The main argument against Howe is that, while he might fix what is broken at United, just as he did at Newcastle, he may lack the final ingredient needed to push the team over the line and deliver a 21st league title. Critics are quick to point out that he never transformed Newcastle into genuine title challengers. Yet that argument is illogical. Despite having some of the richest owners in world football, Newcastle often struggled in the transfer market. Howe wanted the very front three United now possess, Matheus Cunha , Benjamin Šeško and Bryan Mbeumo , but all three rejected the chance to join him. As a result, the Toons endured one of their most disappointing summer windows in 2025. Had Howe secured those players and avoided the injury problems that followed, Newcastle’s 2025-26 campaign could have looked very different. If Jason Wilcox goes ahead and hires Howe, fans will naturally look to him to get the best out of Cunha, Mbeumo and Šeško. Still, one player I believe could be massively revitalised is Joshua Zirkzee . Zirkzee could be Eddie Howe’s Joelinton at Man United When Newcastle signed Joelinton from Hoffenheim in 2019, they were convinced they had secured a centre-forward who would light up the Premier League. Instead, the Brazilian struggled to find the net. There were calls for the Magpies to cut their losses and sign a proven goalscorer. Howe, however, saw something in the Samba star. He recognised Joelinton’s physicality and combativeness, and saw them as perfect for a box-to-box midfield role. It proved a masterstroke. With Joelinton anchoring the engine room, Howe built one of the league’s most formidable midfields, a unit opposition sides genuinely feared. Zirkzee may not possess the same combative edge as Joelinton, yet he shares a similar capacity for reinvention. Deployed in a number 10 role, the Dutchman could flourish. His game is built more around creativity and connection than pure centre-forward play. He excels at receiving the ball under pressure, escaping markers and driving the team forward from deeper positions into the final third. Beyond that, his sharp one-twos and ability to link play could give United a valuable alternative creative outlet on days when Bruno Fernandes is not at his sharpest, as in recent matches. Carrick experimented with Zirkzee in the number 10 role during pre-season, and he was class. However, the United coach has been reluctant to trust him there in competitive fixtures so far. Howe is unlikely to share that caution. In the end, giving Zirkzee a chance to reinvent himself as a playmaker should not only unlock his best qualities but also help the 20-time English champions to hold on to a baller who remains popular in the dressing room and so contributes positively to squad harmony.

item.title: Johnstone To Keep His Place? | Predicted 4-2-3-1 Celtic Lineup To Face Hibernian
item.description: Johnstone To Keep His Place? | Predicted 4-2-3-1 Celtic Lineup To Face Hibernian Despite breaking the deadlock early in the second half, Celtic conceded twice within minutes to Celta Vigo and suffered another European defeat on Thursday night. They now travel to Easter Road to face Hibernian, and the Hoops must take all three points to maintain their cushion at the top of the Premiership. Hibs, stuck at rock bottom in the table, are having a nightmare with just two wins in 9 games. David Gray’s dismissal has not changed their fortune, with new boss Marink Reedijk losing to Dundee United and Falkirk since succeeding the Scotsman. Celtic clinched identical 2-1 wins in Edinburgh when they visited Hibernian last season, and the home side need to punch above their weight to script an upset on Sunday afternoon. Predicted 4-2-3-1 Celtic Lineup To Face Hibernian Defence Martin O’Neill restored Sam Johnstone in goal against Celta Vigo, replacing Viljami Sinisalo. The veteran custodian might now keep his place, having lost it to the Finnish shotstopper following their shambolic 3-0 defeat to Old Firm rivals Rangers before the international break. GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – MAY 10: James Forrest of Celtic shoots at goal during the William Hill Premiership match between Celtic FC and Hibernian FC at Celtic Park on May 10, 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Alistair Johnston is back in team training but must not be rushed into action, given his recurring injury problems. Colby Donovan should get the nod on the right ahead of Anthony Ralston and Jordan Lotomba, but the gaffer could drop Liam Scales and restore Auston Trusty to partner with Dane Murray in deep defence. Kieran Tierney is expected to retain his left-back spot over Landon Emenalo. Midfield Skipper Callum McGregor, a shadow of his earlier self, is likely to feature again as a deep-lying playmaker. The Bhoys lack a like-for-like replacement for the Scottish midfielder, but could rely on versatile Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain to manage his minutes in the middle of the park. Mika Baur must showcase his box-to-box movements and down-the-middle runs while pairing up with McGregor as the ‘double pivot’. Benjamin Nygren has been scrutinised for his lack of work ethic as a ‘number 10’. But the Swedish ace has been consistent with his goals and assists, cementing his spot over Oliver Sorensen and Luke McCowan. Haissem Hassan and Callum Osmand must operate from the flanks; however, the latter’s minutes should be managed carefully as he could not complete the Hearts and Celta fixtures due to fitness reasons. Hyun-jun Yang remains sidelined, but James Forrest, Sebastian Tounekti and Jota could feature from the bench as second-half substitutes. Attack Kasper Hogh should fight for his place, as he lost the starting status to Camilo Duran, who is in flying form while spearheading the attack.

item.title: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has more to say about Lakers star Luka Doncic — ‘He’s not Michael Jordan’
item.description: Justine Willard-Imagn Images Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has more to say about Lakers star Luka Doncic — ‘He’s not Michael Jordan’ appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Golden State Warriors rookie forward Yaxel Lendeborg doubled down on his criticism of Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Doncic on Saturday, declaring that he is not afraid to confront the six-time All-Star because “he’s not Michael Jordan.” Lendeborg addressed his ongoing exchange with Doncic during a locker room interview with Joseph Dycus of The Mercury News ahead of Golden State’s Saturday night matchup against the Phoenix Suns. “I’m not supposed to talk to him, something like that… He gonna say what he wanna say, I’m a say what I wanna say. I’m not afraid to talk to nobody, man. He’s not Michael Jordan , like come on now,” Lendeborg said with a laugh. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 24-year-old rookie also acknowledged that his previous criticism of Doncic might have gone too far. “It’s fun trash talk. I feel like I did kinda take it overboard in the media, but you know it is what it is.” “I’m not supposed to talk to him, something like that… Imma say what I wanna say. I’m not afraid to talk to nobody, man. He’s not Michael Jordan." Yaxel Lendeborg responds to the reactions to his comments about Luka Doncic 👀 (via @joseph_dycus ) pic.twitter.com/4wZk0NzVfN https://t.co/MPjdWD1w3P — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 24, 2026 The exchange follows Lendeborg’s comments after the Warriors suffered a 127-105 season-opening loss to the Lakers on Wednesday night. Yaxel Lendeborg’s Luka Doncic feud adds intrigue to Warriors-Lakers rematch Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Following that defeat, the rookie publicly criticized Doncic’s behavior toward officials during the game. “I had a lot of respect for him [Luka Doncic], but being in there firsthand, watching all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect for him,” Lendeborg said. His latest remarks suggest that while he recognizes his initial comments might have been excessive, he remains unwilling to back down from the Lakers superstar. The developing tension adds another storyline to the rivalry between the two Pacific Division opponents, who will meet again next week. Meanwhile, Golden State enters Saturday’s contest against Phoenix with an 0-2 record after falling 111-108 to the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday night. The Warriors will attempt to secure their first victory of the 2026-27 season when they face the Suns (0-1) at 7 p.m. PT on NBA TV. Golden State will then host Doncic and the Lakers next Friday at 7 p.m. PT on Prime Video, giving Lendeborg another opportunity to face the player he has publicly criticized. Related: Warriors’ Stephen Curry gets 100% real after discouraging loss to Grizzlies Related: Draymond Green calls Yaxel Lendeborg’s technical foul vs. Luka Doncic ‘weakest s*** ever’

item.title: NASCAR qualifying at Talladega sets Sunday lineup for Chase race
item.description: Chase Briscoe and Austin Hill were fastest in Saturday qualifying and have earned the front row for Sunday's YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway. Briscoe averaged 186.065 around the 2.66-mile tri-oval; he was the only driver to surpass 186. Given the nature of big-pack racing at Talladega, Sunday's race has been pointed to as a potential season-wrecker (quite literally) for those within range of winning the Cup Series championship. Where you start at Talladega isn't extremely important, since big chunks of ground can be gathered (and yes, lost) in a matter of seconds, to say nothing of laps. However, since the potential a highly populated crash is always hanging overhead, simple math tells you it's better to have as many cars as possible in your rearview mirror. After a long run of Cup races on the USA network, coverage moves back to NBC this week and for the concluding two weeks, at Martinsville and then the finale at Homestead. item.title: Spurs seal rare win at Chelsea as Palmer sees red
item.description: Tottenham celebrate scoring during their win over Chelsea (Glyn KIRK) Tottenham clinched a Premier League win at Chelsea for just the second time in 36 years as a woeful own goal from Blues keeper Mike Penders was followed by Cole Palmer's red card in Saturday's 2-0 victory. Roberto De Zerbi's side clinched their second successive league win thanks to Penders's howler in the second half at a rain-lashed Stamford Bridge. Chelsea forward Palmer was sent off for a second booking moments later before Mathys Tel produced a superb solo effort to condemn the Blues to their first home defeat against Tottenham since 2018. Since 1990, Tottenham had won just once in 41 previous away matches against London rivals Chelsea in all competitions. Ending that miserable run gave Tottenham only their second win in their last 16 league games against Chelsea, both home and away, and their first since 2023. After a dismal start to the season, Tottenham have climbed to 12th place after building on Monday's win against Coventry, which ended their wait for a first league win this season. It was a bitter blow for fourth-placed Chelsea, who had beaten Bournemouth and Everton in their previous two league games. They were booed off at full-time and remain very much a work in progress under Xabi Alonso in the Spaniard's first season in charge. With Joao Pedro sidelined by a late injury, Morgan Rogers was Chelsea's central striker, but their revamped attack was short of bite. Teed up by Rogers after Pedro Neto stole possession from Mateus Fernandes, Palmer went close to an early opener with a curler that Antonin Kinsky tipped over at full stretch. Tottenham responded with a spell of probing pressure as Omar Marmoush met Andy Robertson's cross with a shot that was repelled by Penders. Alonso's men pieced together the best move of the half with a flurry of one-touch passes to reach Jordan Henderson on the edge of the area, but the midfielder's low drive was palmed away by Kinsky. - Spurs spring a surprise - Neto tested Kinsky with a fierce blast but the Tottenham keeper was up to the task with a save at his near post. Tottenham suffered a blow when often-injured midfielder James Maddison limped off in a premature end to only his second start since May 2025. Maddison had already missed training sessions since his long-awaited start against Coventry and his latest fitness setback suggested it was a failed gamble to start him at the Bridge. In keeping with the sloppy fare, Neto fired straight at Kinsky from a dangerous position after Palmer pounced on Sandro Tonali's wayward pass. item.content:encoded: Tottenham celebrate scoring during their win over Chelsea (Glyn KIRK) Tottenham clinched a Premier League win at Chelsea for just the second time in 36 years as a woeful own goal from Blues keeper Mike Penders was followed by Cole Palmer's red card in Saturday's 2-0 victory. Roberto De Zerbi's side clinched their second successive league win thanks to Penders's howler in the second half at a rain-lashed Stamford Bridge. Chelsea forward Palmer was sent off for a second booking moments later before Mathys Tel produced a superb solo effort to condemn the Blues to their first home defeat against Tottenham since 2018. Since 1990, Tottenham had won just once in 41 previous away matches against London rivals Chelsea in all competitions. Ending that miserable run gave Tottenham only their second win in their last 16 league games against Chelsea, both home and away, and their first since 2023. After a dismal start to the season, Tottenham have climbed to 12th place after building on Monday's win against Coventry, which ended their wait for a first league win this season. It was a bitter blow for fourth-placed Chelsea, who had beaten Bournemouth and Everton in their previous two league games. They were booed off at full-time and remain very much a work in progress under Xabi Alonso in the Spaniard's first season in charge. With Joao Pedro sidelined by a late injury, Morgan Rogers was Chelsea's central striker, but their revamped attack was short of bite. Teed up by Rogers after Pedro Neto stole possession from Mateus Fernandes, Palmer went close to an early opener with a curler that Antonin Kinsky tipped over at full stretch. Tottenham responded with a spell of probing pressure as Omar Marmoush met Andy Robertson's cross with a shot that was repelled by Penders. Alonso's men pieced together the best move of the half with a flurry of one-touch passes to reach Jordan Henderson on the edge of the area, but the midfielder's low drive was palmed away by Kinsky. - Spurs spring a surprise - Neto tested Kinsky with a fierce blast but the Tottenham keeper was up to the task with a save at his near post. Tottenham suffered a blow when often-injured midfielder James Maddison limped off in a premature end to only his second start since May 2025. Maddison had already missed training sessions since his long-awaited start against Coventry and his latest fitness setback suggested it was a failed gamble to start him at the Bridge. In keeping with the sloppy fare, Neto fired straight at Kinsky from a dangerous position after Palmer pounced on Sandro Tonali's wayward pass. When Palmer's run was halted by Fernandes's handball, the Chelsea star escaped with a yellow card after barging into his rival with such aggression that the Tottenham midfielder was sent crashing to the sodden turf. Tottenham exacted swift revenge in the 77th minute. Fernandes's in-swinging corner should have been caught by Penders, but he opted for a punch that was completely mistimed as he diverted the ball into his net for a comical own goal. It was a horrible moment for the 21-year-old Penders, who was making his first league start in the absence of Emiliano Martinez following jaw surgery. Rubbing salt into Chelsea's wounds, Palmer was dismissed three minutes later for an ugly stamp on Conor Gallagher. Tel wrapped up Tottenham's memorable triumph in fitting style in the 87th minute, skipping away from Chelsea's flat-footed defence to drill a fine finish into the bottom corner from the edge of the area. smg/jc

item.title: Köln's René Wagner responds to critique after draw with Schalke
item.description: Köln's René Wagner responds to critique after draw with Schalke Köln managed to keep their first clean sheet this season and also was René Wagner's first clean sheet for Köln in the 0-0 draw with Schalke at home on Sunday. However, the home side controlled possession for the majority of the game and left a fair few chances behind whilst not putting enough pressure on Schalke during periods of the tie. With strikers Ragnar Ache, Thijs Dallinga and Imad Rondić all out with injuries the Billy Goats went through a second game in a row without scoring despite chances including most notably a big chance for substitute Luca Waldschmidt. After the match, the fans in the stadium's infamous Südkurve started whistling and around the ground some unhappy fans started to chant for the manager's exit. Manager René Wagner sympathised partly with this after the tie as he said: “It feels a bit too little to come away from this game with this result.” Wagner was also asked about the reaction from the fans in the stadium after the game but he defended the performance and also the decision to take off winger Mikey Moore. In defending his team and the performance, he said: “It's part of the job to try and win a game like this at home. We felt like we did this but the precision in the final third was not enough.”

item.title: Bristol overcome Exeter to go third in Prem
item.description: Gabriel Ibitoye had a key influence in both of Bristol's tries [Shutterstock] The Prem Bristol (10) 20 Tries: Ibitoye, Ivanishvili Cons: Williams 2 Pens: Williams 2 Exeter (0) 7 Tries: Fisilau Cons: Slade Bristol moved up to third place in the Prem after beating Exeter 20-7 at Ashton Gate. Gabriel Ibitoye's 26th-minute try and James Williams' penalty three minutes later were the only scores of an attritional first half in difficult conditions. Greg Fisilau was mauled over 12 minutes after the restart as Exeter got on the scoreboard. The Chiefs tried to force a second, but it was Bristol that earned the win when Williams kicked an excellent 41-metre penalty before Luca Ivanishvili crashed over from close range after Olly Woodburn had fumbled a high ball. His late try denied Exeter a losing bonus point and leaves Rob Baxter's side in ninth place on eight points, six behind the Bears. Resurgent Tigers overpower Saints in derby downpour 'That's what I do' - Wade scores again to equal Prem try-scoring record The stormy weather's impact was in evidence from the first whistle as both sides struggled to keep hold of the ball. Bristol almost scored in the opening 60 seconds after an Exeter mistake under a kick saw the ball bobble around in their in-goal area. It was as close as either side came to scoring in the opening 26 minutes as the hosts had the better of the possession and territory but were stifled by a spirited Exeter defence. The pressure finally told when Ibitoye got on the end of a looping Harry Randall pass and beat Zack Wimbush to dive into the left corner. Williams' penalty soon after extended the lead to 10 points and Exeter then had Australia star Tom Hooper forced off with a shoulder injury just before the interval. Despite that setback, Henry Slade almost dotted down a Sam Wolstenholme grubber kick four minutes after the restart before Exeter's maul got them back into the game soon after. First the pack earned themselves a penalty and the second maul from the resulting lineout 10 metres out saw Fisilau forced over. The Chiefs forwards won another penalty inside the 22 with eight minutes left, but superb work from Ibitoye saw the Bears turn the ball over six metres out. Bristol went straight up the field and a penalty resulting from a high tackle was dispatched well by Williams despite the tough conditions. And the weather proved to be a distraction for Woodburn soon after as he missed a high kick and was put under pressure by Ibitoye, who was stopped inches from the Exeter line. But eight phases later Georgian replacement Ivanishvili forced his way over to seal a hard-fought victory. item.title: How Dunlap girls tennis team, and its star player, finished in IHSA state finals
item.description: Anna Yu's season ended just short of the medal round in the 2026 IHSA girls state tennis finals. The Dunlap junior lost in the Class 2A consolation state semifinals on Saturday, Oct. 23 at Buffalo Grove High School. Her season came to a close with a 6-3, 6-2 defeat to New Trier junior Ingrid Fielder, who had already held a championship bracket third-round victory over Yu. Despite the loss, Yu earned second-team All-State honors and a top-8 finish in her first foray into the Class 2A state finals. She is the two-time reigning Journal Star Player of the Year and was the Class 1A state runner-up last season. Dunlap was 15th in the team standings as a first-time Class 2A participant. 2026 IHSA girls tennis results, schedule for Peoria area Class 2A Singles Anna Yu (Dunlap, jr.) Consolation - Semifinals: Ingrid Fielder (New Trier, jr.) def. Yu 6-3, 6-2 Consolation - Quarterfinals: Yu def. Enya Neagu (Barrington, jr.) 6-3, 6-3 Consolation - Round 5: Yu def. Maya Keller (Highland Park, fr.) 6-2, 6-4 Consolation - Round 4: Yu def. Jennifer Tang (Neuqua Valley, soph.) 6-0, 6-2 Championship - Round 3: Ingrid Fielder (New Trier, jr.) def. Yu 4-6, 6-1, 6-1 Championship - Round 2: Yu def. Maddie Hrtanek (Rolling Meadows, jr.) 6-1, 6-1 Championship - Round 1: Yu def. item.title: Dortmund beat Frankfurt to go top in Bundesliga
item.description: Borussia Dortmund's Maximilian Beier (2nd R) celebrates scoring his side's first goal with teammateS during the Bundesliga soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and Eintracht Frankfurt at Signal Iduna Park. (is associated with: «Dortmund beat Frankfurt to go top in Bundesliga») Bernd Thissen/dpa Borussia Dortmund returned to winning ways in the Bundesliga with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday to top the table for at least one night. Two substitutes eventually made the difference after Frankfurt had held firm for a long time, as Maximilian Beier curled the winner in the 80th minute off Jobe Bellingham. Dortmund, who had drawn their two previous league matches, moved three points ahead of champions Bayern Munich who play at third-placed Freiburg on Sunday and will go top again with victory before hosting Dortmund next weekend. Serhou Guirassy had a dangerous shot in the 15th minute saved by Frankfurt goalkeeper Noah Atubolu. Guirassy should have scored two minutes later one on one against the keeper but Atubolu prevailed again with his right arm. A deflected shot from Daniel Svensson hit the top of the bar, but Frankfurt almost stole a 34th minute lead when a mistake from Felix Nmecha saw Younes Ebnoutalib with only Gregor Kobel to beat but couldn't get the ball past him. Kobel tipped a shot from Fares Chaibi over the bar shortly after the restart before Guirassy came even closer at the other end when his header off a corner kick hit the crossbar in the 53rd. Beier came on in the 68th and Bellingham in the 79th. A minute later, the two combined for Beier to curl into the right corner from the edge of the area for a late victory. In earlier Saturday action, RB Leipzig trounced Elversberg 4-0, Werder Bremen won 3-2 at Mainz, Paderborn defeated SV Hamburg 1-0, Augsburg and Union Berlin drew 1-1 and there were no goals at Cologne v Schalke. Borussia Dortmund's Ramy Bensebaini (L) and Eintracht Frankfurt's Jonathan Burkardt battle for the ball during the Bundesliga soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and Eintracht Frankfurt at Signal Iduna Park. (is associated with: «Dortmund beat Frankfurt to go top in Bundesliga») Bernd Thissen/dpa

item.title: José Mourinho responds to Barcelona star’s criticism
item.description: José Mourinho responds to Barcelona star’s criticism Real Madrid head coach José Mourinho has on Saturday provided his response to the recent criticism aimed in the direction of he and Los Blancos by Barcelona star Fermín López. Real Madrid and Barcelona are of course primed to renew rivalries on Sunday evening, in the season’s first edition of El Clásico. In the buildup to the fixture, much of the media chatter has centred on developments away from the pitch, as those in a position of power at the Santiago Bernabéu continue to seek punishment for their Camp Nou counterparts for their part in the ‘Negreira Case’. Drawn on as much in the days leading up to the fixture, Barcelona midfielder Fermín López admitted: “Real Madrid’s constant references to the Negreira case are getting a bit tiring because we’re showing our quality on the pitch. It’s unfair to engage in this kind of rhetoric when things are going well for us. If they keep pushing this narrative, it’s because it suits them, but we don’t get involved in it.” Speaking during his pre-match press conference on Saturday, it therefore came as little surprise when the subject of Fermín’s comments was put to the aforementioned José Mourinho. And Real Madrid’s headmaster sniped back, in assuring: “There are other things that exhaust us, but they keep happening…” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: SSC Napoli vs Roma: The tactics board - Balerdi and McTominay exchange blows in chaotic six-goal stalemate
item.description: SSC Napoli v AS Roma - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport A tactical masterclass in mid-block stability met its match in chaotic second-half verticality as SSC Napoli and Roma played out a thrilling 3-3 draw. While Massimiliano Allegri focused on midfield late-runs, Gian Piero Gasperini’s bench proved decisive in salvaging a point. Massimiliano Allegri entered this fixture with a clear mandate: restore defensive equilibrium to a Napoli side that had lacked balance in the opening weeks. His tactical blueprint focused on a disciplined mid-block, designed to frustrate Roma’s possession-heavy approach while exploiting the half-spaces through late runs from his dynamic midfield trio. The objective was to force Roma into wide areas and then punish them on the transition through the pace of Hoejlund and the technical ingenuity of De Bruyne. In contrast, Gian Piero Gasperini’s Roma arrived at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona intent on dominating the ball and stretching the pitch. With over 60% possession, the Giallorossi aimed to overload the central channels and use their wing-backs to pin Napoli’s full-backs deep. However, the first half showcased a significant struggle for Roma to convert their 24 total shots into high-quality chances, as Napoli’s compactness forced them into low-percentage efforts from distance. SSC Napoli's tactical setup Allegri deployed a fluid 4-3-3 system that morphed into a 4-5-1 during defensive phases. The inclusion of Scott McTominay and Frank Zambo Anguissa alongside Kevin De Bruyne provided a blend of physical dominance and creative vision. The primary pressing trigger was activated when the ball reached Roma’s central midfielders; Napoli would immediately collapse inward to cut off passing lanes. This was evident in the 28th minute when Anguissa capitalised on a lapse in central coverage to open the scoring. In the build-up, Napoli eschewed risky short passing from the back, often looking for direct vertical balls toward Hoejlund to bypass Roma’s initial press. McTominay’s role was particularly sophisticated; he functioned as a "shadow striker," ghosting into the box to exploit the space created by the wingers pinning the Roma centre-backs. This tactical nuance resulted in two goals for the Scotsman, who repeatedly found himself unmarked in the area. Defensively, Napoli remained narrow, allowing Roma to have the ball in wide areas while ensuring that the central zone remained a congested fortress, making clear-cut opportunities for the visitors difficult to come by until the final stages. Roma's tactical setup Gasperini opted for his signature 3-4-2-1, a formation designed to create numerical superiorities across the pitch. Roma’s build-up play was patient, involving the three central defenders and Marten de Roon, who dropped deep to act as a pivot. The width was provided by the wing-backs, whose high positioning forced Napoli’s Politano and Lang to track back, effectively turning Napoli’s 4-3-3 into a 6-3-1 at times.
item.content:encoded: SSC Napoli v AS Roma - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport A tactical masterclass in mid-block stability met its match in chaotic second-half verticality as SSC Napoli and Roma played out a thrilling 3-3 draw. While Massimiliano Allegri focused on midfield late-runs, Gian Piero Gasperini’s bench proved decisive in salvaging a point. Massimiliano Allegri entered this fixture with a clear mandate: restore defensive equilibrium to a Napoli side that had lacked balance in the opening weeks. His tactical blueprint focused on a disciplined mid-block, designed to frustrate Roma’s possession-heavy approach while exploiting the half-spaces through late runs from his dynamic midfield trio. The objective was to force Roma into wide areas and then punish them on the transition through the pace of Hoejlund and the technical ingenuity of De Bruyne. In contrast, Gian Piero Gasperini’s Roma arrived at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona intent on dominating the ball and stretching the pitch. With over 60% possession, the Giallorossi aimed to overload the central channels and use their wing-backs to pin Napoli’s full-backs deep. However, the first half showcased a significant struggle for Roma to convert their 24 total shots into high-quality chances, as Napoli’s compactness forced them into low-percentage efforts from distance. SSC Napoli's tactical setup Allegri deployed a fluid 4-3-3 system that morphed into a 4-5-1 during defensive phases. The inclusion of Scott McTominay and Frank Zambo Anguissa alongside Kevin De Bruyne provided a blend of physical dominance and creative vision. The primary pressing trigger was activated when the ball reached Roma’s central midfielders; Napoli would immediately collapse inward to cut off passing lanes. This was evident in the 28th minute when Anguissa capitalised on a lapse in central coverage to open the scoring. In the build-up, Napoli eschewed risky short passing from the back, often looking for direct vertical balls toward Hoejlund to bypass Roma’s initial press. McTominay’s role was particularly sophisticated; he functioned as a "shadow striker," ghosting into the box to exploit the space created by the wingers pinning the Roma centre-backs. This tactical nuance resulted in two goals for the Scotsman, who repeatedly found himself unmarked in the area. Defensively, Napoli remained narrow, allowing Roma to have the ball in wide areas while ensuring that the central zone remained a congested fortress, making clear-cut opportunities for the visitors difficult to come by until the final stages. Roma's tactical setup Gasperini opted for his signature 3-4-2-1, a formation designed to create numerical superiorities across the pitch. Roma’s build-up play was patient, involving the three central defenders and Marten de Roon, who dropped deep to act as a pivot. The width was provided by the wing-backs, whose high positioning forced Napoli’s Politano and Lang to track back, effectively turning Napoli’s 4-3-3 into a 6-3-1 at times. This territorial dominance yielded 11 corners and 24 shots, yet Roma lacked the clinical edge to break Allegri’s resolve early on. The pressing game from Roma was intense and high, aiming to win the ball back within seconds of losing it. However, the high line left them vulnerable to Napoli’s quick transitions. Soulé and Malen operated in the pockets of space between Napoli’s midfield and defence, looking to turn and drive at the back four. While they struggled to penetrate for an hour, the tactical insistence on recycling possession eventually wore down the Napoli rearguard. The defensive shape relied heavily on the recovery pace of N'Dicka and Hermoso, but they were frequently caught out by the timing of McTominay’s late arrivals into the penalty area. The tactical chess match The primary tactical battle centered on the half-spaces and the management of McTominay’s vertical runs. For much of the match, Allegri appeared to be winning this duel. By allowing Roma to have sterile possession (61%), Napoli conserved energy and struck with surgical precision on the counter. The mismatch occurred when Roma’s double pivot failed to track McTominay’s movement from deep, leading to his goals in the 48th and 83rd minutes. Allegri’s decision to prioritise central density over ball retention seemed to have secured the points. However, Gasperini eventually won the battle of endurance. By maintaining a high volume of crosses (35 compared to Napoli’s 16) and constant pressure, Roma eventually broke the physical resolve of the Napoli defenders. The tactical victory for Gasperini lay in his refusal to deviate from his attacking principles, even when trailing 2-0. The sheer weight of Roma’s offensive output - producing 2.64 Expected Goals (xG) - suggested that their tactical dominance was real, even if the finishing was initially absent. In-game adjustments The match was transformed by Gasperini’s triple substitution in the 58th minute. The introduction of Leonardo Balerdi, Santiago Castro, and Nahuel Molina injected fresh energy and a more aggressive profile into the Roma side. Balerdi’s introduction was a tactical masterstroke; primarily a defender, he was pushed forward during set-pieces and chaotic sequences, exploiting Napoli’s fatigue to score twice in the final 15 minutes. This shift to a more desperate, direct approach disrupted Napoli’s organised mid-block. Allegri attempted to counter this by bringing on Stanislav Lobotka and Leonardo Spinazzola to regain control of the tempo and provide fresh legs on the flanks. However, these changes were reactive rather than proactive. The move to a more defensive posture invited further Roma pressure, culminating in Balerdi’s 89th-minute equaliser. The shift in momentum was prompted by Napoli’s inability to maintain their pressing intensity, as evidenced by Roma’s late dominance in the air and their success in second-ball situations. Gasperini’s willingness to throw caution to the wind with his defensive substitutes ultimately salvaged the draw. Conclusion Ultimately, the outcome was decided by the clash between Allegri’s structured counter-attacking and Gasperini’s relentless offensive volume. While Napoli’s tactical plan to use McTominay as a goal-scoring weapon was executed perfectly, they failed to account for the physical toll of defending for 90 minutes against a team with Roma’s territorial dominance. Gasperini’s bench - specifically the unexpected goal-scoring threat of Balerdi - exposed Napoli’s late-game fragility. In a game of fine margins, Roma’s persistence and tactical flexibility in the final third proved just enough to negate Napoli’s clinical transition play.

item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There were times when Roberto De Zerbi’s frustration threatened to boil over. The Tottenham manager cut a tense figure in his technical area. He bounced around for 90 minutes and let out blasts of fury whenever he saw something that displeased him, but in the end he was able to celebrate leading Spurs to their first win at Stamford Bridge since 2018. It was not a pretty game. It was not a good game. The breakthrough was a comedy own goal from Mike Penders. The young Belgian goalkeeper, deputising for the injured Emi Martínez, was culpable when Spurs went ahead, flapping at a corner from the excellent Mateus Fernandes and punching the ball into his own net. Jacob Steinberg’s full report to follow Continue reading...

item.title: UFC 333 live blog: Alexander Volkov vs. Rizvan Kuniev
item.description: Alexander Volkov and Rizvan Kuniev ahead of UFC 333﻿ | Jeff Bottari, Zuffa LLC This is the UFC 333 live blog for Alexander Volkov vs. Rizvan Kuniev, the main card heavyweight bout Saturday at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. The matchup pits two top 10 contenders against one another, with Volkov at No. 4 and Kuniev at No. 9 in the MMA Fighting Global Rankings. Volkov (40-11) has made a strong case for a title shot with back-to-back wins over Waldo Cortes-Acosta and Jailton Almeida to make it six victories in his past seven fights. His lone loss during that stretch was a contentious split decision loss to Ciryl Gane, who is set to defend his recently elevated undisputed title against Josh Hokit at UFC 334 on Nov. 14. Can Volkov finally secure a championship opportunity if he gets past Kuniev? In just three UFC appearances, Kuniev (14-3-1, 1 NC) has broken out from the middle of the pack, earning his ranking with wins over Almeida and Tyrell Fortune. Outside of a split decision loss to Curtis Blaydes in his UFC debut, Kuniev has been nearly unbeatable since 2017, though his run is marred by a positive drug test during his time with PFL in 2023. Kuniev looks to shake up the rankings and break into the top 5 with a win over Volkov. Check out the UFC 333 live blog for Alexander Volkov vs. Rizvan Kuniev below. Preamble Ok, we’re now on four-fight finishing streak following Aaron Pico’s incredible showing — and all in the first round. Will the big boys get things done quickly in Abu Dhabi? We’re watching you guys, Volkov and Kuniev. These two Russian heavyweights have trained together (briefly) in the past and the tension has been boiling through interviews over the past few days, so this one could be explosive. Round 1

item.title: Supersub Beier ends Dortmund's winless run with late winner against Frankfurt
item.description: Supersub Beier ends Dortmund's winless run with late winner against Frankfurt Borussia Dortmund momentarily climbed to the top of Bundesliga standings after their narrow win over Eintracht Frankfurt. Niko Kovac beat his former club after his side lost top spot in the wake of uninspiring draws with Werder Bremen and Union Berlin. With their former legendary coach Jürgen Klopp in attendance, Dortmund started the game on a positive note. Noah Atubolu’s first save came in the 15th minute from a decent effort by Serhou Guirassy, who ended the Black and Yellows goal drought with a brace at Sabah in the Champions League. A couple of minutes later, the Guinean striker failed in his attempt to chip Atubolu with an even bigger chance. The hosts continued their pressure as Nnamdi Collins saved by the woodwork from beating his own goalkeeper in the half-hour mark. At the other end, Felix Nmecha's mistake presented a golden opportunity for Younes Ebnoutalib, but Gregor Kobel pulled a save from Frankfurt's first big chance. Adi Hütter's side settled into the game after that, with Nmecha's injury-time effort the only chance the hosts created for the rest of the half. There was a slight delay at the start of the second-half because of fireworks. Guirassy had the first chance of the half as Dortmund hit the woodwork for the second time. Kovac's side had a total of 13 corner-kicks in the game, but they hardly create goal scoring opportunities from them. With only ten minutes left on the clock, Jobe Bellingham registered an assist in his first action of the game as fellow substitute Maximilian Beier broke the deadlock with a brilliant finish. The makeshift wingback also scored Dortmund's winner against Stuttgart on matchday 4. Frankfurt will now face HSV in back-to-back games as their cup tie will follow a matchday 8 encounter. Kovac's men will host the in-form Werder Bremen for the second time this month before next week's showdown against FC Bayern.
