item.title: Man City's perfect start ended by Aston Villa, Arsenal go joint-top
item.description: Manchester City were beaten for the first time in the Premier League this season (Darren Staples) Manchester City's flawless start to the Premier League season was ended in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday that allowed Arsenal to join them at the top of the table with victory over Everton. Tottenham won at Chelsea for just the second time in 42 visits to Stamford Bridge as Mike Penders's own goal and a Cole Palmer red card cost the Blues in a 2-0 defeat. Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City's struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons. Nicolas Jackson struck twice for Unai Emery's men to continue a fine run of form for a new-look Villa side. Erling Haaland briefly levelled early in the second half, but Maresca was left to rue City not making more of their dominance for large spells of the game. "We lost because we probably are not being clinical enough in their box," said Maresca. The Villa side that won the Europa League last season was decimated by high-profile departures during the transfer window. But Emery has quickly moulded his new squad into shape with Jackson proving his critics from a difficult spell at Chelsea wrong. The Senegal international pounced on an error by Marc Guehi to fire Villa ahead after just six minutes. Another of Villa's new signings Zion Suzuki then thwarted City with a string of stunning saves. Haaland headed in his 13th goal in 10 games this season to equalise. Villa, though, swiftly responded as Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to keep out Jackson's low shot on the hour mark. "A fantastic day to share with our supporters in Villa Park," said Emery. "We felt that this is our fortress and the energy the supporters gave us was really fantastic." - Arsenal's set-piece prowess - Arsenal took advantage to move alongside City on 21 points from eight games with a routine 2-0 win against Everton. Shorn of the creative inspiration of Bukayo Saka, who is set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines with a thigh injury, Arsenal had to rely on their set-piece prowess to get the job done. Ezri Konsa bundled in his first goal for the club after Everton failed to clear a corner to open the scoring on seven minutes. Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the lead for Mikel Arteta's men midway through the second period. "We had some problems to finish the actions but we scored from a set-piece," said Arteta. "That gave us the confidence and composure to go and dominate the game." Tottenham climbed out of the bottom three as Chelsea self-imploded at the Bridge. A game hampered by wild weather conditions exploded into action in the final 15 minutes when, on his first Premier League start, Penders, deputising for the injured Emi Martinez, miscued his attempted punch from a Spurs corner over his own line. A game hampered by wild weather conditions exploded into action in the final 15 minutes when, on his first Premier League start, Penders, deputising for the injured Emi Martinez, miscued his attempted punch from a Spurs corner over his own line. Moments later Palmer was dismissed for a second yellow card after catching former team-mate Conor Gallagher. Spurs took full advantage as Mathys Tel's low strike also deceived Penders to win for only the second time at their London rivals since 1990. Fulham also moved out of the relegation zone with a 1-0 win at Coventry thanks to Oscar Bobb's individual effort. On Sunday the focus turns to Manchester United boss Michael Carrick when his side take on Bournemouth. A seven-game winless streak has plunged Carrick's future into doubt just months after he was hired on a two-year deal after a successful interim spell in charge at the end of last season. kca/ea/jc/nf

item.title: Beier late show sends Dortmund top of Bundesliga
item.description: Werder Bremen's Niclas Fuellkrug has scored in six straight Bundesliga games. (Kirill KUDRYAVTSEV) Maximilian Beier scored in the 80th minute to send Borussia Dortmund top of the Bundesliga table after a hard-fought 1-0 home win over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday. In a game lacking clear chances, Jobe Bellingham came off the bench and threaded a clever pass for fellow substitute Beier to score less than a minute later. The narrow victory was Dortmund's first in the league since mid-September and took Niko Kovac's side three points clear atop the Bundesliga table. Bayern Munich can return to the top of the table with a win at Freiburg on Sunday but will be without coach Vincent Kompany, who is being treated in hospital for a mystery virus after collapsing at training on Friday. Dortmund had started the season with a run of six straight wins but came into Saturday's game in a mini slump, having won just one of their past four in all competitions. The best opportunity of the first-half fell to Serhou Guirassy with 15 minutes gone. The Guinean was one on one with Noah Atubolu but tried a soft chip, which the goalkeeper palmed away. Just after the break, Guirassy headed a Joey Veerman corner against the bar. Beier came on for the ineffective Fabio Silva with 22 minutes remaining. With 10 minutes left, Beier collected a Bellingham pass and curled in the winner from just inside the box. It was the second time in four league games Beier was the only scorer in a 1-0 Dortmund win. - Fuellkrug 'shines bright' - Niclas Fuellkrug scored for the sixth straight Bundesliga match as his Werder Bremen side won 3-2 at Mainz. Fuellkrug, who returned to Bremen on loan from English Championship side West Ham in the summer, converted two penalties inside the opening 25 minutes to notch up a second straight Bundesliga brace. Ludovit Reis grabbed Bremen's other goal, while Anthony Caci and Lee Jae-sung scored for the hosts. Fuellkrug now has eight goals this season, half of his total in his final campaign in Bremen in 2022/23, when he won the Bundesliga top-goalscorer award. The Germany striker scored just three goals during an injury-hit 18-month spell at West Ham and just one in a six-month loan at AC Milan. Bremen coach praised his in-form striker, telling reporters: "You can tell that he feels comfortable. "He is our guiding star -- and he's shining brightly right now. He's carrying this team along with him." RB Leipzig rebounded from their 4-1 thumping away at Real Madrid midweek with a comfortable 4-0 home win over promoted Elversberg. Romulo scored a double while Tidiam Gomis, who scored Leipzig's only goal at the Bernabeu, and Christoph Baumgartner also got on the scoresheet as the Saxons climbed to fifth. Without a point away from home, Leipzig have now won their four home games by a collective score of 18-0. item.title: Aidan Hutchinson Called Secret Lions Meeting That May Have Saved Detroit’s Defense
item.description: The Detroit Lions entered their bye week feeling considerably better about their defense following a dominant performance against the Arizona Cardinals. But what fans didn’t know was that Aidan Hutchinson had taken matters into his own hands just days before Detroit delivered its most complete defensive effort of the season. Following an ugly start to the year, Hutchinson organized a players-only meeting that brought Detroit’s entire defensive unit together for an important conversation. There were no coaches directing the discussion, no elaborate speeches, and no attempts to single out struggling teammates. Instead, Hutchinson and several veteran leaders wanted to address something that had quietly become a problem. The Lions had stopped playing with the confidence and freedom that once helped define their defense. And with Sunday’s NFC North showdown against the Green Bay Packers approaching, Detroit’s players believe that meeting could prove to be a turning point. Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (97) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Aidan Hutchinson Takes Charge After Lions’ Defensive Struggles The numbers through Detroit’s first four games were difficult to ignore. The Lions had surrendered an average of 31.8 points per game, and defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard’s unit was struggling to prevent opponents from moving the football through the air. Following Detroit’s 32-26 loss to Carolina, Hutchinson decided something needed to change before the team’s problems became more difficult to correct. According to reporting detailing Hutchinson’s players-only meeting , the Pro Bowl edge rusher contacted fellow defensive leaders and helped organize a gathering that included players from every position group. Among those who spoke were Alim McNeill, Derrick Barnes, Jack Campbell, and D.J. Reed . The message wasn’t about changing defensive schemes or questioning Sheppard’s leadership. It was about restoring communication, trusting assignments, and remembering why they loved playing football. Barnes admitted the defense had become too tense while attempting to correct its early-season mistakes. “I feel like everybody’s ass was tight,” Barnes said in comments documented by Dave Birkett. “Players, everybody. item.content:encoded: The Detroit Lions entered their bye week feeling considerably better about their defense following a dominant performance against the Arizona Cardinals. But what fans didn’t know was that Aidan Hutchinson had taken matters into his own hands just days before Detroit delivered its most complete defensive effort of the season. Following an ugly start to the year, Hutchinson organized a players-only meeting that brought Detroit’s entire defensive unit together for an important conversation. There were no coaches directing the discussion, no elaborate speeches, and no attempts to single out struggling teammates. Instead, Hutchinson and several veteran leaders wanted to address something that had quietly become a problem. The Lions had stopped playing with the confidence and freedom that once helped define their defense. And with Sunday’s NFC North showdown against the Green Bay Packers approaching, Detroit’s players believe that meeting could prove to be a turning point. Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (97) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Aidan Hutchinson Takes Charge After Lions’ Defensive Struggles The numbers through Detroit’s first four games were difficult to ignore. The Lions had surrendered an average of 31.8 points per game, and defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard’s unit was struggling to prevent opponents from moving the football through the air. Following Detroit’s 32-26 loss to Carolina, Hutchinson decided something needed to change before the team’s problems became more difficult to correct. According to reporting detailing Hutchinson’s players-only meeting , the Pro Bowl edge rusher contacted fellow defensive leaders and helped organize a gathering that included players from every position group. Among those who spoke were Alim McNeill, Derrick Barnes, Jack Campbell, and D.J. Reed . The message wasn’t about changing defensive schemes or questioning Sheppard’s leadership. It was about restoring communication, trusting assignments, and remembering why they loved playing football. Barnes admitted the defense had become too tense while attempting to correct its early-season mistakes. “I feel like everybody’s ass was tight,” Barnes said in comments documented by Dave Birkett. “Players, everybody. Coaches.” The veteran linebacker explained that players needed to stop putting so much pressure on themselves and start enjoying the game again. Detroit Lions Respond With Their Best Defensive Performance The results against Arizona were difficult to overlook. Detroit entered its Week 5 matchup determined to simplify its approach and play with greater confidence, and the difference was immediately noticeable. The Lions recorded five sacks against Jacoby Brissett , limited the Cardinals to just 56 rushing yards, and forced five consecutive three-and-outs during their commanding 45-21 victory. More importantly, the defense appeared energized throughout the afternoon. Players celebrated big plays, communicated more effectively, and played with the kind of collective confidence that had been missing during the opening month. As we previously reported following Detroit’s victory over Arizona , head coach Dan Campbell had plenty of reasons to celebrate after his team delivered one of its strongest overall performances of the season. However, what made the defensive improvement especially meaningful was that the motivation came directly from the players. Defensive lineman Tyler Lacy acknowledged that the meeting helped restore the group’s energy, particularly when it came to celebrating and supporting one another on the field. McNeill also emphasized that the players wanted to correct their problems before they became a recurring issue. The veteran defensive tackle believed the meeting was necessary because Detroit still had plenty of time to turn things around. Packers Will Provide Much Bigger Test for Lions Defense While the Cardinals game offered encouragement, the Lions cannot assume one impressive performance means their defensive problems have been solved. Detroit still ranks near the bottom of the NFL in several major defensive categories, including points allowed, passing yards, total defense, and third-down efficiency. And Green Bay presents challenges that Arizona simply could not. The Packers lead the NFL with eight completions of at least 40 yards, and quarterback Jordan Love has several dangerous weapons capable of exploiting breakdowns in Detroit’s secondary. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden provide significant downfield speed, while the expected return of running back Josh Jacobs could give Green Bay another dimension offensively. The Packers’ own breakdown of Sunday’s matchup highlights Detroit’s impressive pass rush, which has produced a league-leading 20 sacks through five games. That makes Hutchinson’s leadership particularly important. The Lions have proven they can pressure opposing quarterbacks, but that pass rush must work together with a secondary that has frequently struggled to maintain coverage. One missed assignment against Love could quickly turn into a game-changing touchdown. Brian Branch’s Return Could Make Hutchinson’s Message Even More Important Detroit should also receive a major boost with Brian Branch nearing his first appearance of the season. The talented defensive back has been recovering from a torn Achilles suffered last December, leaving the Lions without one of their most versatile defensive playmakers. As we previously reported in Detroit’s final Week 7 injury update , Branch is officially listed as questionable against Green Bay despite making significant progress during practice. If he plays, Branch could provide another experienced voice and a much-needed upgrade in coverage. But his presence alone won’t solve everything. Hutchinson’s meeting was about making all 11 defenders responsible for their assignments, trusting the players around them, and eliminating the hesitation that had plagued Detroit earlier this season. That philosophy becomes even more important against an offense capable of stretching the field and forcing defenders into difficult decisions. For the Lions, Sunday’s matchup is an opportunity to demonstrate that their performance against Arizona wasn’t simply the result of facing an overmatched opponent. Aidan Hutchinson may have helped Detroit rediscover its defensive identity behind closed doors. Now the Lions must prove they can carry that identity onto the field against one of their biggest rivals.

item.title: Payton Tolle’s season debut against the Yankees solidified his roster slot, probably forever
item.description: Before we begin looking ahead to 2027, OTM is looking back at 2026, highlighting some of the biggest, strangest, and most memorable moments of a memorable season. Today, we look back at the belated season debut of a new rotation mainstay. So much was made of Brayan Bello’s redemption arc — a spring demotion to Triple-A followed by a subsequent rebirth as a dominant bulk reliever — that many (including this writer) briefly forget that an even better starter actually began 2026 in Triple-A. The 2026 Red Sox roster was notable for how awesome the rotation looked in March. It was rife with the presence of a recent Cy Young runner-up in Garrett Crochet, Bello, who was fresh off the World Baseball Classic, Ranger Suarez, who was an exciting addition to the top of the rotation from Philadelphia, another addition in Sonny Gray, and Connelly Early, who looked amazing even in defeat in 2025’s Wild Card Round at Yankee Stadium. That, of course, left a couple guys on the outside looking in, including Payton Tolle, who himself pitched in the waning moments of last season. If there was any internal competition between the two young guns, it was manufactured if it existed at all. The duo took pictures together, were inseparable on broadcasts, and had nothing but praise for each other. Tolle, a towering lefty just like his newfound best friend and rotation-mate Early, had his four-seam fastball in spades. He also had one of the best call-up videos I have ever seen prior to his first start against eventual NL Cy Young winner Paul Skenes on August 29 (featuring a WooSox manager he surely would never see again, right?) While Tolle had his fastball, though, he lost ground to Early in the early going of each’s career with the amount of times he was taken over an outfield wall; 5 in 18 innings, to be exact, in comparison to Early avoiding that feat in his 19 innings. That was probably the defining factor in the decision to give Early his first Opening Day roster nod in what will, in all likelihood, become a successful career… in Washington, amongst other places, as Tolle, after a 2026 campaign that saw him notch 171 strikeouts and pitch to an ERA just a hair over 3, is a lock to capture his first Opening Day slot in 2027. So how did we get here? We can look at April 23 at Yankee Stadium as a pivotal point. The Red Sox had just gotten a good 3 2/3 innings in relief out of Eduardo Rivera, who had never pitched higher than Double-A in his short professional career. item.content:encoded: Before we begin looking ahead to 2027, OTM is looking back at 2026, highlighting some of the biggest, strangest, and most memorable moments of a memorable season. Today, we look back at the belated season debut of a new rotation mainstay. So much was made of Brayan Bello’s redemption arc — a spring demotion to Triple-A followed by a subsequent rebirth as a dominant bulk reliever — that many (including this writer) briefly forget that an even better starter actually began 2026 in Triple-A. The 2026 Red Sox roster was notable for how awesome the rotation looked in March. It was rife with the presence of a recent Cy Young runner-up in Garrett Crochet, Bello, who was fresh off the World Baseball Classic, Ranger Suarez, who was an exciting addition to the top of the rotation from Philadelphia, another addition in Sonny Gray, and Connelly Early, who looked amazing even in defeat in 2025’s Wild Card Round at Yankee Stadium. That, of course, left a couple guys on the outside looking in, including Payton Tolle, who himself pitched in the waning moments of last season. If there was any internal competition between the two young guns, it was manufactured if it existed at all. The duo took pictures together, were inseparable on broadcasts, and had nothing but praise for each other. Tolle, a towering lefty just like his newfound best friend and rotation-mate Early, had his four-seam fastball in spades. He also had one of the best call-up videos I have ever seen prior to his first start against eventual NL Cy Young winner Paul Skenes on August 29 (featuring a WooSox manager he surely would never see again, right?) While Tolle had his fastball, though, he lost ground to Early in the early going of each’s career with the amount of times he was taken over an outfield wall; 5 in 18 innings, to be exact, in comparison to Early avoiding that feat in his 19 innings. That was probably the defining factor in the decision to give Early his first Opening Day roster nod in what will, in all likelihood, become a successful career… in Washington, amongst other places, as Tolle, after a 2026 campaign that saw him notch 171 strikeouts and pitch to an ERA just a hair over 3, is a lock to capture his first Opening Day slot in 2027. So how did we get here? We can look at April 23 at Yankee Stadium as a pivotal point. The Red Sox had just gotten a good 3 2/3 innings in relief out of Eduardo Rivera, who had never pitched higher than Double-A in his short professional career. Garrett Crochet was, to put it bluntly, not pitching well, but it would not be revealed until later in the week that he was actually dealing with shoulder inflammation that would place him on the Injured List for the remainder of the season. Thus, Alex Cora needed a starter for the third game at Yankee Stadium on Friday night on Apple TV, and who better than a guy who was mowing them down in Worcester to face Cam Schlittler? The game started out as a duel. Tolle looked every bit up to the challenge. After three consecutive balls in the exact same spot to Amed Rosario, Tolle came back in the count. K. He then sat Aaron Judge down on four pitches. And that fastball would bite Ben Rice, clocking in at 98. He’d then get Giancarlo Stanton and Randal Grichuk. Five hitters, five strikeouts. Tolle was back, and he was here to stay. In fact, he’d not allow a baserunner until the fourth inning. View Link All told, Tolle would wrap up his night confidently, even with allowing a home run to Jazz Chisholm. His 3 up, 3 down in the sixth including two strikeouts, number 10 and number 11 on the night, finished his outing. It would be the most strikeouts a Red Sox pitcher had on the season until Sonny Gray tied it in Colorado two months later; Tolle would eventually have the title on the team with 14 against the Athletics. Sadly, Alex Cora made a few managing mishaps that would define the beginning of the 2026 season and would do him in. The signature tells were both in effect here, but one was no fault of his: the offense wouldn’t really support the good start out of Tolle outside of a Carlos Narvaez home run, and Cora’s part in the loss was calling on Greg Weissert with inherited runners (from Danny Coulombe) when there was plenty of evidence that those inherited runners would score. And score they did – the final score: Yankees 4, Red Sox 2. The Yankees would complete the sweep against the Red Sox, take the season series, and end the Red Sox season some months later. That was Tolle’s best night for a couple of months, and some of his tells still existed. He still allowed home runs at a higher rate than most of the other rotation. But he went deep into games and certainly struck guys out. Every team wants a pitcher that gives them a real chance to win. After July 7, the team would be on the losing end of a Tolle start just twice in the regular season. The encouraging news, even with the fifth consecutive loss at Yankees Stadium, is that, on that fateful night in the Bronx, the Red Sox’s rivals had no answer for a guy who hopefully will be a foundation of the rotation for years to come.

item.title: Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham: Late double gives Spurs win against 10-man Chelsea
item.description: Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham: Late double gives Spurs win against 10-man Chelsea Tottenham Hotspur picked up their first win at Stamford Bridge since April 2018 this evening, as they beat an out of sorts Chelsea 2-0. It took until the 77th minute for the deadlock to be broken, and it wasn’t even an attacking player who put the ball in the net. Instead, it was Mike Penders who punched the ball into his own goal, having misjudged the flight of a corner. It went from bad to worse for Chelsea when Cole Palmer was shown a second yellow card, and subsequently a red, with 10 minutes left to play. Spurs’ second came late in the day when Mathys Tel broke free down the left flank and fired past Penders to secure a vital win for his side. As it happened Chelsea made two changes from their 2-0 win over Everton last time out, with Emiliano Martinez missing out due to a fractured jaw sustained in that match and Joao Pedro not in the Blues’ squad. They were replaced by Penders and Geovany Quenda. Spurs also made two changes, with Tel and Mateus Fernandes replacing Dominic Solanke and Tosin Adarabioyo. The first 15 minutes were a “feeling-out period” for both sides before Palmer’s left-footed strike was well saved by Antonín Kinský. Mohammed Kudus was the first Spurs player to really threaten the Chelsea goal, when a similar effort to Palmer’s drifted wide of the far post. Penders’ first save of the evening came just shy of the half-hour mark, getting down fast to deny Omar Marmoush from close range. The Belgian was called into action again just two minutes later, this time racing off his line to smother Tel’s shot. The end-to-end action continued when Kinský was forced into a superb double save to deny Jordan Henderson and Pedro Neto, though the latter was offside. Sandro Tonali was next up to try and break the deadlock for the Lilywhites, but he was unable to keep his strike on target from the edge of the area, meaning it remained 0-0 at the break. James Maddison appeared to go down with an injury early in the second half, and he was replaced by former Chelsea midfielder Conor Gallagher. Pedro Neto latched on to a poor back pass on the hour mark, forcing a save from Kinský. However, Xabi Alonso’s side were unable to make the resultant corner count. Alonso turned to his bench minutes later, introducing Marco Palestra in favour of Jorell Hato. Meanwhile, Solanke and Pedro Porro replaced Marmoush and Andy Robertson. Gallagher was shown the first yellow card of the match in the 67th minute, when he pulled back Morgan Rogers just inside Spurs’ half. He was very quickly joined by Palmer, who reacted to a poor challenge from Fernandes as the Englishman looked to break in behind. Fernandes and Roberto De Zerbi were also booked. Chelsea’s second change saw Quenda replaced by Estevão as the Blues looked to break the deadlock. The Brazilian made an immediate impact, driving into the Spurs box before firing into the side netting. The deadlock was finally broken in the 77th minut

item.title: Let’s Argue: Chiefs need to improve or will go .500 the rest of the way
item.description: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images In our “Let’s Argue” series, Mark Gunnels considers the hot takes, wacky predictions and unpopular opinions of Kansas City Chiefs fans from all over the world. 5crawfishdinners says: If our average level of play doesn’t improve over the first five games, we’ll go .500 over the last 12 games I disagree because one thing we’ve learned about the Chiefs over the years is that they tend to play down to their competition, but they also know how to elevate their game when the stakes are higher. You can’t just look at their average level of play and assume that’s what you’ll get every week, especially against the better teams in the league. This team has consistently shown it can flip that switch when it matters most. bgack says: Chiefs win Super Bowl over the 49ers I can definitely see Chiefs-49ers Part 3 in the Super Bowl. These are arguably the two most complete teams in football, and both have the coaching, talent, and experience to make another deep postseason run. But until San Francisco proves it can beat Mahomes when it matters most, I’m rolling with Kansas City AGAIN. aadicker says: The Chiefs’ first loss of the season will be against the Falcons I agree the Buffalo Bills are the biggest threat because Josh Allen will always make them dangerous, especially in January. But I’m not sleeping on the Jacksonville Jaguars either — they’ve got enough talent on both sides of the ball to be a real problem in the AFC. That said, if the Chiefs get to the postseason healthy with Mahomes, an improved running game, and a defense that keeps developing, I’ll take my chances against anybody. CleverlyNamed says: We do not need another WR and trading for one midseason will not move the needle much I disagree because while I don’t think the Chiefs necessarily NEED another receiver, that doesn’t mean adding the right guy wouldn’t move the needle. If a legitimate difference-maker becomes available, why wouldn’t you explore it, especially when you’re trying to maximize another Super Bowl window with Patrick Mahomes? There’s a big difference between making a move just to make one and adding a weapon who could take this offense to another level.
item.content:encoded: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images In our “Let’s Argue” series, Mark Gunnels considers the hot takes, wacky predictions and unpopular opinions of Kansas City Chiefs fans from all over the world. 5crawfishdinners says: If our average level of play doesn’t improve over the first five games, we’ll go .500 over the last 12 games I disagree because one thing we’ve learned about the Chiefs over the years is that they tend to play down to their competition, but they also know how to elevate their game when the stakes are higher. You can’t just look at their average level of play and assume that’s what you’ll get every week, especially against the better teams in the league. This team has consistently shown it can flip that switch when it matters most. bgack says: Chiefs win Super Bowl over the 49ers I can definitely see Chiefs-49ers Part 3 in the Super Bowl. These are arguably the two most complete teams in football, and both have the coaching, talent, and experience to make another deep postseason run. But until San Francisco proves it can beat Mahomes when it matters most, I’m rolling with Kansas City AGAIN. aadicker says: The Chiefs’ first loss of the season will be against the Falcons I agree the Buffalo Bills are the biggest threat because Josh Allen will always make them dangerous, especially in January. item.title: “A great feeling” Ezri Konsa enjoyed scoring and keeping a clean sheet
item.description: “A great feeling” Ezri Konsa enjoyed scoring and keeping a clean sheet Ezri Konsa scored one of Arsenal’s goals as the Gunners defeated Everton in the Premier League this afternoon , and the defender was delighted with his contribution to the victory. The Englishman joined Arsenal from Aston Villa in the summer and has quickly become one of the club’s most reliable players. His defensive consistency has strengthened the squad, while his performances have demonstrated why he is regarded as one of the Premier League’s leading defenders. Konsa attracted interest from top clubs after several impressive seasons at Aston Villa. He moved to the Emirates just weeks after winning the Europa League with Villa, arriving at Arsenal with a strong reputation and expectations that he could make an immediate impact. Konsa enjoys a memorable evening Arsenal have been pleased with Konsa’s performances since his arrival, and scoring while helping the team keep a clean sheet made the victory against Everton particularly special. The defender was delighted to contribute at both ends of the pitch as the Gunners secured all three points. His goal also rewarded his persistence, as he revealed that he had been waiting for an opportunity to score from a set piece. Speaking after the match, Konsa explained how much the result and his personal contribution meant to him. He told Premier League Productions : “It is a great feeling to get the three points, it always is. A clean sheet and a goal; it is a fantastic day overall. “I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I set to the set-piece coach before the game and he said he had been waiting for it as well. It was only right I got it today. A goal from a set piece has felt like it has been coming. Today was the day. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Defender praises Gabriel Konsa also praised Gabriel for helping him settle into life at Arsenal. The pair have developed a strong understanding, and the Englishman appreciates the support he has received from his defensive partner since joining the club. “I’m pleased for Gabriel. He is a top player and a top human. He has made my life easy since I joined the club and it is a pleasure to play along side him.” The victory was therefore a satisfying occasion for Konsa, who contributed a goal, helped secure a clean sheet and recognised the teammate who has made his transition to Arsenal easier. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Allegri enraged after Napoli 3-3 Roma: ‘Maybe I shouldn’t be on the touchline’
item.description: Allegri enraged after Napoli 3-3 Roma: ‘Maybe I shouldn’t be on the touchline’ Max Allegri was extremely agitated in post-match interviews after his red card in Napoli’s 3-3 thriller with Roma . ‘Maybe I shouldn’t even be on the touchline from now on.’ The coach saw red for dissent after the Giallorossi equaliser for 3-3, as he and his players felt Sam Beukema was fouled by Leonardo Balerdi in the build-up to the Argentina international’s decisive header. It was the culmination of an epic battle, which saw the Partenopei surge into a 2-0 lead through Andre Frank Zambo Anguissa and Scott McTominay, then Roma fought back with Matias Soulé and Balerdi goals in the space of five minutes. McTominay had drilled from distance to restore the lead at 3-2 only for that last-gasp Balerdi header. Allegri fuming after Napoli thriller NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Massimiliano Allegri, SSC Napoli head coach, reacts to his expulsion during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) “The fourth official called the referee and got me sent off, but I said absolutely nothing,” Allegri told DAZN Italia. “Next time I will have to sit on the bench and not move, because every time I move, I get sent off. I had to pay €80,000 in fines last season, so maybe I shouldn’t even be on the touchline from now on. I see others who practically run onto the pitch and nobody says anything, when I move, I’m punished. “I thank the fourth official Saccani, and for the rest, I can only congratulate the lads for their performance,” he added with sarcasm. NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Matias Soule of AS Roma celebrates after scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Napoli fans are increasingly frustrated with the number of goals that they are leaking, as they already lived through a 4-3 victory over Bodo/Glimt here in the Champions League midweek. “I think this evening the team played well, also defensively, against a strong side. We had the chance to go 3-0 up, we then had the lead at 3-2, but conceded again. If we play with this spirit, we will climb the table,” noted Allegri. It was put to the coach that conceding this many goals is frankly very unusual for someone of his tactical approach, as he has always been famous for being defensive. “I changed my way of playing now, it is all on the attack. Since the start of the season, I even try to use four strikers if I can,” he again added with sarcasm. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Napoli picked up just one point from the last two Serie

(Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Napoli picked up just one point from the last two Serie A rounds, losing 3-1 at rock bottom Venezia and then fumbling this lead for a 3-3 draw with Scudetto contenders Roma. It also means they have not managed two wins on the bounce in all competition yet this season. “Unfortunately, we’ve dropped a lot of points along the way, I’m still angry at the way the game ended, so I’m perhaps lacking sharpness in evaluating how the match went. I’m sorry, but after 25 years of this, I can make mistakes too.” NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Massimiliano Allegri SSC Napoli head coach during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Rasmus Hojlund has now not scored in eight competitive appearances for Napoli, so how can he put this crisis behind him? “He had three very favourable situations this evening, he worked for the team, which was not easy. He had a header in the first half, another couple of situations, so the goal will arrive eventually.” NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Massimiliano Allegri, SSC Napoli head coach, reacts to his expulsion during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Benoit Badiashile limped off with a muscular issue in the second half. “Unfortunately, he had this injury and we will evaluate it over the next 48 hours.” Allegri was asked if he sees the glass half-full or half-empty at Napoli after his 3-3 result. “I don’t know, you tell me if it’s half-full or half-empty. I am in no condition right now, for the first time after 25 years, to give you any clear answers on the match. So I’m sorry, but I have to wish you a good night.”

item.title: Game Thread: Michigan State @ UCLA
item.description: EAST LANSING, MI - OCTOBER 10: Michigan State mascot, Sparty, dances at midfield before a college football game between the Michigan State Spartans and Illinois Fighting Illini on October 10, 2026 at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, MI. (Photo by Adam Ruff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Game #8 is today and it is in a stadium that many of us Spartan fans have some wonderful memories of. Unfortunately, this matchup is not an earned bowl game at the end of a highly accomplished MSU season. Rather, our 2-5 squad is playing conference foe UCLA and their perfect 6-0 record. The Bruins have been playing at a high level while MSU is dealing with a high level of injuries . The game starts at 3:30 PM ET and is airing on CBS. It’s Saturday; let’s get rowdy! item.title: Preview: Bournemouth vs. Liverpool
item.description: LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 20: Alexis Mac Allister of Liverpool celebrates scoring his team’s third goal with teammate Kostas Tsimikas during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Liverpool FC and Villarreal CF at Anfield on October 20, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images) | Liverpool FC via Getty Images LIVERPOOL VS. BRIGHTON & HOVE ALBION | Sunday, October 25th | Premier League | Anfield 2:00PM BST/10:00AM EST Liverpool are coming off of three good results in the Champions League and Premier League as they welcome Brighton and Hove Albion to Anfield. The Reds are still looking to earn their first victory and three points at home after two draws and a loss. It will be a tough one, against a Brighton side that have gotten off to a great start and currently sit in third place on the table. They’ve already earned clean sheets in their last five games, including a 3-0 victory over Arsenal. They’ve also scored 23 goals in their first seven league games. Alexander Isak has already scored five goals in the first six games, so the team will rely on him to continue his good form and create chances to beat Brighton’s currently high-flying defense. However, the big news isn’t about the teams or any specific players, but the weather. Storm Boelo could bring heavy wind, rain, and even flooding to Merseyside before Sunday’s match. While it has not been postponed yet, it’s a possibility as of right now. Maybe that heavy wind could aim itself towards Brighton’s goal and help out a little if it does go on. Predicted Liverpool Lineup (4-2-3-1) Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Nyoni, Mac Allister; Barcola, Wirtz, Ngumoha; Isak Andoni Iraola continues to navigate serious early season injury concerns. This week, he’ll be without Jeremie Frimpong, Dominik Szoboszlai, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley, Victor Muňoz, and poor Giovanni Leoni. That’s quite the annoying list considering it’s not even Halloween. Good news is that Bradley Barcola should be available. For Hürzeler and Brighton, they’ll be without Evan Ferguson, Stefanos Tzimas, Kaoru Mitoma, Femi Azeez, and Zadok Yohanna. Jason Steele, Pascal Struijk, Yankuba Minteh, and Mats Wieffer are doubts. The Managers Have Their Say Andoni Iraola : “They are doing incredibly well. They deserve all the praise they are getting and I think there is little doubt that it is a team that is very well coached. Very good in every phase of the game; without the ball they are one of the best teams and also with the ball they have good quality. We need to be at our very best because right now they have confidence – but I also see my team in a good place.” Fabian Hürzeler : “We know what we can expect from Liverpool. Very intense pressing so a very intense game. Anfield is always a very special environment and atmosphere. We have to be prepared mentally and physically, but we seem to be in a good place.” The Officials Referee: Sam Barrott. Assistants: A

item.title: L’Jarius Sneed traveling separately to Seatle; Chiefs make 4 roster moves
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 14: Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed #38 of the Kansas City Chiefs tackles wide receiver Pat Bryant #13 of the Denver Broncos during the first quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before departing for a Week 7 road game against the Seattle Seahawks on “Sunday Night Football,” the Kansas City Chiefs made four roster moves on Saturday. We have signed Practice Squad player RB Jaydn Ott to an active roster contract. We have activated LB Cooper McDonald from Reserve/Injured. We have activated Practice Squad player WR Justin Watson via Standard Elevation. We have placed RB Brashard Smith on Reserve/Injured. pic.twitter.com/fZX4YNjghi — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) October 24, 2026 The team is adding a defensive reinforcement in second-year linebacker Cooper McDonald, who has been on the team’s Reserve/Injured (IR) list since leaving Week 1’s contest against the Denver Broncos with a knee injury. The Chiefs designated McDonald to return to practice this week, and he drew a questionable tag on this week’s final injury report . Now that he has been put back on the active roster, the Chiefs removed his game designation for Sunday night. On Friday, head coach Andy Reid confirmed that third string running back Brashard Smith would be listed as out for Sunday due to a hamstring injury and that practice squad rookie Jadyn Ott would make his NFL debut in his place. That will apparently be the status for the next month. Rather than a practice squad elevation, Ott has been signed to the 53-man roster with Smith heading to IR. Smith will be out for at least Kansas City’s next four games. Veteran wide receiver Justin Watson did receive a practice squad call up for this week’s contest. Watson returned to the Chiefs earlier this month, where he played from 2022-24. He signed to the practice squad in the wake of injuries to wideouts Tyquan Thornton and Rashee Rice. Thorton is likely out for the season after dislocating his ankle in Week 4. Rice will miss his second consecutive contest on Sunday with a hamstring injury. Watson — who was released by the Houston Texans before the season — was elevated in Week 6 to suit up against the Los Angeles Chargers . He played only one offensive snap in his season debut and did not see a target. He also played three special teams snaps. CB L’Jarius Sneed is not traveling with the team today (personal) but will meet the team in Seattle. Sneed’s game status remains Questionable with a knee injury. item.title: Championship roundup: Southampton beat West Ham; QPR put five past Swansea
item.description: Hammers humbled at home; Swansea thrashed 5-0 Burnley sack manager Hayen after 4-1 loss at Lincoln Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham . Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin were all on target in a chaotic first half, while Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers. Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. Southampton, deducted four points at the start of the season, are now just two points behind West Ham. Continue reading...

item.title: Scottish Premiership: Kelsy fires Rangers to emphatic win; Dundee United pip Aberdeen
item.description: Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone; Dundee United 3-2 Aberdeen Kevin Kelsy scores two to sink 10-man Saints Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 Premiership win at Ibrox. After dropping two points at Dundee last Saturday , the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy. Saints started the second half brightly but goals from Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by referee Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on midfielder Nico Raskin, before substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining. Continue reading...

item.title: Clinical Arsenal earn precious win against Everton thanks to Konsa and Gabriel
item.description: The wait goes on for David Moyes. The 63-year-old Scot must have been hoping that on his 14th visit to this stadium as Everton’s manager, his luck would change. Yet from the moment Ezri Konsa slammed home his first goal for Arsenal as the Premier League champions rediscovered their knack of scoring from set pieces, the writing was on the wall. While it took until midway through the second half for Gabriel Magalhães to make sure of the victory, Arsenal were never going to let slip the chance of moving level on points at the top with Manchester City after their defeat by Aston Villa earlier in the day. Continue reading...

item.title: Nicolas Jackson double sees Aston Villa end Manchester City’s perfect start
item.description: Manchester City added a loss in the Premier League to one to the Premier League, as their perfect record this season vanished without an independent commission in sight. Two of the most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side came out on top against Erling Haaland. City are certainly fallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games. Mistakes cost City as Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma were punished by Jackson, who will have taken great pleasure in ending the winning run of his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca. Continue reading...

item.title: Vincent Kompany to miss ‘weeks, not days’ with virus treatment, say Bayern Munich
item.description: Head coach in hospital after collapsing in training Assistant coach Aaron Danks to take charge against Freiburg Bayern Munich expect Vincent Kompany to miss an extended period as their head coach continues his hospital treatment for a virus after collapsing on the training pitch on Friday. Speaking at a press conference on Saturday, Bayern’s sporting director, Max Eberl, confirmed Kompany was still in hospital in a stable condition. Kompany’s English assistant coach, Aaron Danks, will replace the 40-year-old for Sunday’s Bundesliga match at Freiburg. Eberl said examinations were continuing to determine the nature of the former Manchester City and Belgium captain’s condition, with a recovery timeframe yet to be determined. Continue reading...

item.title: Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásico
item.description: Once Bobby Robson’s translator at the Camp Nou, José Mourinho is tasked with bringing down Barcelona on Sunday José Mourinho has done the por que?, the printout and the press conference no-show, and he’s been here only three months. The Real Madrid manager has played the classics without even playing a clásico. Not yet anyway, but it’s time: on Sunday night he returns to the stadium he first arrived at 30 transformative years ago as Bobby Robson’s talented young translator, and last visited in 2013 as the most famous manager in football. The coach who once declared “today, tomorrow and always, Barcelona in my heart,” and claimed he would only ever go to Real Madrid to destroy them, has been entrusted with attempting to bring about the destruction of Barcelona. It is not the first time: if his return is about nostalgia, which it is, that’s wrapped up in their rivals too. Continue reading...

item.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
item.description: Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer. Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result. Continue reading...

item.title: NWSL drops controversial criteria around ‘Rodman Rule’ in settlement with NWSLPA
item.description: Any player will be eligible for High Impact Player status Requirements had included top 100, marketability lists Sides also resolve grievance on Rodman contract refusal The NWSL and the NWSL Players Association have reached a settlement to drop the restrictive criteria around the controversial High Impact Player (HIP) rule, allowing any player to earn the league’s highest salaries. The NWSL introduced the rule late last year, allowing teams to spend an additional $1m above the salary cap to sign star players. Players with the designation had to meet one of eight criteria, ranging from US national team minutes and Ballon d’Or recognition to NWSL Best XI honors to media lists, including the Guardian’s Top 100 and a ranking that ordered athletes by marketability. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. item.dc:creator: Rob Smyth
item.content:encoded: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart
item.description: Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. EA Continue reading...

item.title: Slegers and misfiring Arsenal badly need a result in WSL north London derby
item.description: Gunners’ title hopes have seemingly evaporated and their under-pressure head coach faces her latest test against Spurs on Saturday It says much about Arsenal’s predicament that the team who have conceded 12 goals in two games are not the side whose head coach is under most pressure before a north London derby. Tottenham, four points above their neighbours before Saturday’s meeting, may have been humbled in consecutive Women’s Super League matches but all eyes are on Renée Slegers. Arsenal are winless in five WSL matches for the first time, and the most decorated club in English women’s football desperately need a turning point. Their failure to beat Birmingham at home last Saturday, dropping points against a promoted side for the second time this season, again demonstrated the team’s inability to convert possession into goals. They increasingly look like a team stuck in Groundhog Day. Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
